articleTitle: PrivFED: Protecting User Privacy in Federated Learning Systems Through Differential Privacy
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This research examines the integration of Federated Learning (FL) with differential privacy (DP) to enhance privacy protection in distributed machine learning systems. We propose and implement a comprehensive privacy-preserving framework PRIVFED that addresses the growing challenges of data privacy while maintaining model utility. Through extensive experimentation using the MNIST dataset, we demonstrate that our approach achieves significant privacy improvements with minimal performance degradation. Our results show that moderate privacy protection (ε= 1.0) achieves 92.4% accuracy, while strong privacy protection (ε = 0.5) maintains 88.7% accuracy compared to the baseline of 98.2%. Furthermore, our system shows efficient scaling with increasing number of clients, introducing only 15.3% computational overhead. The proposed PRIVFED framework adapts dynamically to varying privacy requirements and data distributions, making it suitable for real-world applications across healthcare, financial services, and critical infrastructure sectors. This work establishes that machine learning systems can achieve both strong privacy guarantees and high model performance, providing practical guidelines for privacy-preserving distributed learning implementations in sensitive domains.

articleTitle: Benchmarking the DC Performance of Tree-Shaped NSFETs for Low Power Logic Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: In this work, we systematically evaluated the DC performance of Tree-shaped NSFET using a fully calibrated 3-D TCAD simulator. Various crucial DC parameters, such as drive current, off current, switching ratio ION/IOFF, Drain Induced Barrier Lowering (DIBL), Threshold voltage, and Subthreshold Swing (SS), have been evaluated at the device level. The Tree-shaped NSFET's transfer and output characteristics have also been investigated. The main findings are ION of 10–5 A, IOFF of10-12A, SS values of 72.037 mV/dec, Vth of 0.318 V, and a higher ION/IOFF ratio (>108), respectively. Furthermore, we also discussed the impact of scaling the gate length and inter-bridge's width (WIB) and height (HIB) on device performance.

articleTitle: Towards Lightweight Hybrid Deep Learning Approach to Malware Detection Enhancement For IoT Based Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: With rapid growth in use of smart devices and internet of things (IoT) the risk of cyber attacks has also been raised. Light weight machine learning methods to identify and stop cyber-attacks has become a topic of interest for the research community. Such systems are constrained in resources so they require light weight models that can operate in low resource environment. This work presents the parameters that support in determining if the model can be considered as light weight model. This work also contributes a unique light weight deep learning model combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU) over federated architecture. The research presents promising results to counter the malware attacks with real-world publicly accessible IoT network dataset, the study assessed the performance of the model using Aposemat IoT-23 dataset. We achieved around 96% and validation accuracy reaching 0.94% with 5 epoch. The results of this work shall contribute to advance deep learning approaches in cybersecurity and provide insightful analysis for the construction of more flexible and robust malware detection systems.

articleTitle: Enhanced Maize Cultivation: IoT Based Precision Agriculture System
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Maize is a vital staple crop that requires precise nutrient management to achieve optimal growth and yield. Traditional agricultural practices often lead to inefficient resource utilization and in-creased environmental degradation. We propose an innovative system to improve maize cultivation in response to challenges. Our system employs an autonomous rover with a camera and dew nodes, which have soil sensors to monitor soil temperature, pH, NPK levels, and moisture content. The rover collects and transmits these data, monitors air temperature and humidity, and displays them on an LCD screen. The rover and dew nodes communicate through a wireless internet-independent system. The data collected are analyzed using machine learning models to predict soil health, providing actionable insights to farmers for efficient fertilizer application. Our system offers significant advantages, including improved resource efficiency and crop yield through precise, data-driven management.

articleTitle: Harnessing Machine Learning for Watermarking: A Survey on Robustness and Stealth in Image Protection
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: In recent years, the rapid growth of digital media has raised concerns over the protection of intellectual property rights. Image watermarking has emerged as a key technique for embedding copyright information into digital images. Traditional methods, such as spatial and frequency domain watermarking, often struggle with robustness against attacks like compression, noise, and resizing. However, machine learning (ML) has shown great promise in enhancing the effectiveness of watermarking systems by improving both robustness and imperceptibility. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the application of machine learning techniques in image watermarking, categorizing key approaches, evaluating their strengths and weaknesses, and discussing potential future directions.

articleTitle: Design of a Triple Band Microstrip Patch Antenna and Its Performance Enhancement using Triple Band AMC for Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This work presents a triple-band patch antenna with a novel connected triple triangular ring shape geometry. The antenna is designed on flexible Teflon glass substrate of permittivity 2.1 and lost tangent 0.0003 with dimensions of 0.4x0.096 λo2, hence well suited for wearable applications. The proposed antenna designed to work on the ISM and Satellite band of applications at 2.4 GHz, 5.5 GHz and 8 GHz, respectively. A novel capacitive coupling feeding is imposed to get better impedance matching at the resonance bands. The gain performances of the proposed wearable antenna are further improved by incorporating a three element jerusalem cross shaped slot as Artificial Magnetic Conductor (AMC) beneath the antenna. The gain performance has improved to a maximum of 7.5 dB at the frequency of 3.2 GHz with incorporating the AMC in the antenna. Thus, this design can be well suited for many wearable applications at those bands.

articleTitle: The MARVEL Dataset: Marine Debris Analysis and Recognition for Vision-Based Exploration
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Aquatic ecosystems are at risk from marine debris, but current databases are not diverse enough to detect it accurately in the real world. We fill this void by presenting the MARVEL (Marine Debris Analysis and Recognition for Vision-Based Exploration) dataset, which is intended to categorize various forms of waterborne garbage, including shopping bags, plastic particles, rotting fruits, and thermocol. The distinct features of marine debris are not captured by existing datasets such as TrashNet and MJU-garbage, which mostly concentrate on general garbage. In order to guarantee precise classification for reliable model training, our dataset contains carefully annotated photos using the LabelMe tool. Vision-based detection systems are improved by the MARVEL dataset, increasing their efficacy in practical applications. It enables improvements in marine pollution control and aids in international efforts to protect aquatic ecosystems by addressing a crucial research gap.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Five Level Cascaded H Bridge SPWM Inverter Fed Five Phase Induction Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This Research in multilevel inverter is ramping up due to the growing demand for more energy-efficient systems. Multi-level Inverter fed Induction Motor drive is one of the most useful technique for controlling the different parameter of multiphase drive. The five-level cascaded H bridge SPWM inverter-fed five-phase induction motor drive is modeled and simulated in the MATLAB/Simulink environment in this article. Because of its advantages over alternative topologies Cascaded H Bridge SPWM (Sinusoidal Pulse Width Modulation) based inverter technique is employed in this paper. The goals of this effort are to enhance power quality and lower the THD content. D-q reference frame theory model based five phase induction motor is fed by CHB inverter to observe the performance analysis of different parameters of five phase induction motor.

articleTitle: MRI-Scan Based Brain Tumor Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Brain tumor extraction and its analysis are challenging tasks in medical image processing because brain image is complicated. The doctor's primary responsibility is to find the tumor, which takes a lot of time and causes them stress. Computer vision is important in the field of human health because it lessens the need for human judgement to produce correct results. The three most popular and secure magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) imaging techniques are CT, X-ray, and MRI scans. MRI can identify even the smallest items. Datasets are used for training, testing, and validation. Our gadget will determine whether or not the subject has a brain tumor. Accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity are some of the performance indicators that will be used to analyse the final results.

articleTitle: Real Time Brown Spot Disease Detection in Paddy Crop Using Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Paddy cultivation is critical to India's economy, providing a living for millions. Brown spot disease, a common fungal illness, can cause significant crop loss if left untreated. Given the high cost and environmental effect of pesticides, early diagnosis is critical for reducing their use. In this study, the modified YOLOv9 model is used to provide a deep learning-based approach for brown spot disease detection in rice leaves at an early stage. YOLOv9's end-to-end architecture enables quicker inference while maintaining accuracy. In this work brown spot paddy images data-set is collected that were labeled with RoboFlow. This work uses Deep Learning model to train the dataset, enabling real-time object detection with fewer computational resources. YOLOv9 beats RCNN as well as YOLOv8, YOLOv7, YOLOv5 etc., in terms of speed and efficiency, enabling real-time object identification with less computer resources. This method exhibits the potential for precise and efficient brown spot identification, which can lead to better pest control and agricultural yields.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Triangular-Circular Microstrip Patch Antenna with Two Switches
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a 5G reconfigurable microstrip patch antenna, having differently shaped dual patches, that is capable of operating in multiple 5G frequency bands. Four design scenarios are investigated, including a single radiating patch, a dual radiating patch, a dual radiating patch with a switch, and a dual radiating patch with two switches. The switches enabled the antenna to reconfigure and operate in two different 5G frequency bands, covering the n79 band (4.4 - 5 GHz) and the high 5G sub-6 GHz frequency band range (4.8 - 6 GHz). The simulated results show that the antenna achieves a resonant bandwidth of 5 GHz and 5.02 GHz for the single and dual patch designs, respectively, 4.29 GHz and 5.2 GHz for one RLC switch-enabled design, and finally, 4.42 GHz, 4.85 GHz, and 5.37 GHz for the two RLC switch-enabled design.

articleTitle: Dynamic RGB Filter on a Metaverse-Based Museum for Color Blind User
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Color blindness is a condition that affects the cone cells in the eyes, either congenital or acquired, and is classified as a moderate disability impacting a portion of the global population. This condition poses significant challenges to visual experiences, particularly in accessing digital facilities such as the metaverse. This paper explores the expansion of facilities for individuals with disabilities to access metaverse-based platforms using Oculus Quest. Dynamic RGB filters in Unity3D and Spatial.io were implemented in this study as accessibility features for metaverse-based museum environments. A key challenge in this context is ensuring accessibility for colorblind visitors who may struggle with accurate color perception. The proposed method enables colorblind users to select from various filters that modify camera colors to enhance color differentiation based on specific types of color blindness. These filters, encompassing eight types of color blindness, aim to improve visual experiences and accessibility for colorblind individuals within virtual museum environments.

articleTitle: News Sentiment Analysis in Financial Markets: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: In recent years, the integration of sentiment analysis into financial markets has gained considerable attention, particularly through the use of machine learning and deep learning techniques. This survey explores the progress and challenges in applying these models to analyze news sentiment and its impact on market behavior. The work describes a comparison of recent deep learning architectures, such as Long Short-Term Memory, Convolutional Neural Networks, and hybrids in comparison to more traditional approaches of machine learning such as Support Vector Machines and Random Forest. The experiments indicated that the deep learning technique generally performed better than those conventional techniques, particularly where the model used a pre-trained language model. This work offers a comprehensive overview of the current state of development in financial news sentiment analysis and points out areas for further research in making models more robust and accurate.

articleTitle: Enhanced Performance of Software Defined Network (SDN) Through Meta Heuristic Particle Swarm Optimization Random Forest Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Integration of Software-defined Networking (SDN) with traditional networking technologies is crucial due to the increasing demand for network performance. SDN offers a centralized and programmable solution for managing the network, while legacy networking systems provide stability and compatibility with existing infrastructures. However, integrating these two systems often results in suboptimal network performance. The Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Random Forest (RF) algorithm is suggested in this research as a potential solution to this problem of network performance improvement in SDN-legacy network integration. PSO and RF are metaheuristic algorithms that have been successfully applied to many optimization problems, including network optimization. The proposed solution used PSO to optimize the routing of packets in the SDN-legacy network, resulting in improved network performance and reduced latency. Simulation outcomes demonstrate the success of the proposed solution and show that it outperforms existing solutions in terms of network performance. When the outcomes are contrasted with other field-wide algorithms already in use, it is found that PSO and RF perform better than the competitors. The results show that PSO-RF decreases end-to-end delay and enhance the performance from 99% to 100% compare to other meta-heuristic algorithms.

articleTitle: Optimal Capacitor Placement and Sizing by Controlling Reactive Power in Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This article is about the optimization and sizing of capacitor and its placement in distribution network to enhance the voltage stability and reduce the power losses. By finding weak buses and placing the shunt capacitor at those buses, it's possible to improve the efficiency while reducing the cost. The teaching-learning based optimization (TLO) has been hybridized with PSO which is a simple and non-complex approach for finding out capacitor placement points, minimize loss and cost for maximum optimization. This algorithm is applied for capacitor placement and sizing by working in two different phases “Teacher Phase” and “Learner Phase” which has been introduced in PSO for position and velocity update to reduce the power loss and cost. TLO helps to improve the PSO based solution to make it more refined and optimum. As a result, the TLO-PSO algorithm successfully minimizes the power losses and capacitor placement costs iteratively refining optimal capacitor locations and sizes. Results show progressive improvement through nearly 100 iterations, converging towards an optimal solution. The effectiveness of TLO-PSO is validated in addressing power system inefficiencies and in achieving cost-effective, stable, and efficient voltage profiles across the distribution network.

articleTitle: Embedding-Based Framework for Disaster Tweets Classification With Explainable AI Insights for Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Societies are significantly impacted by disasters; fast and accurate information is needed in order to respond. Despite challenge like unstructured data and fake news, Twitter can be used in sharing real-time updates. This paper focuses on a robust framework for categorizing disaster-related tweets using dense embeddings such as GloVe, BERT, and FastText, along with machine learning models like Support Vector Machine, Decision Tree, XGBoost, Gradient Boost, Light GBM, Multi-layer Perceptron. The GloVe embeddings with SVM model outperformed all of the other models with an accuracy of 90.09%. LIME and SHAP analyses are implemented to evaluate the significance of each word in a given tweet in order to provide insights into their contributions to model's prediction.

articleTitle: Enhancing Sar Operations with UAV's in Remote Areas: A Lorawan-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: To increase efficiency and shorten response time, search and rescue operations in distant and inaccessible places require advances in technology. Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have emerged as essential aids in these missions, providing real-time monitoring, a longer operational range, and more accuracy in locating individuals in distress. This research focuses on the integration of reliable transceivers for long-distance communication with a high-accuracy human-detecting model. The research addresses critical issues in rescue missions by analyzing LoRa based transceiver efficiency and obtaining significant detection accuracy using advanced algorithms. The paper presents a methodology for integrating LoRaWAntransceivers for efficient data transfer and analyzing their performance parameters. In addition, a super-efficient rescue algorithm is provided, which improves decision-making and mission execution in critical situations, paving the way for enhanced UAV-based rescue solutions.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Machine Learning Models for Diabetes Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Diabetes is one of the most widespread and critical health issues globally, attributed to factors such as obesity, sedentary lifestyles, and elevated blood sugar levels. These factors disrupt insulin function, resulting in metabolic irregularities and increased glucose concentrations in the bloodstream. This research aims to address the rising prevalence of diabetes by leveraging machine learning techniques to predict its onset. By providing early warnings, this approach seeks to motivate individuals to adopt healthier dietary and lifestyle choices, potentially reducing the risk of developing diabetes. The performance of several machine learning algorithms, such as classification and ensemble learning techniques, is investigated in this paper. K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Random Forest, Decision Tree, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression, XGBoost algorithm, Neural Network, and Ensemble learning voting classifier are some of the important methods that were assessed. Complementary preprocessing techniques, such as Label Encoding, Feature Engineering, replacing missing values, train-test split methods, are used to prepare and analyze the data. These methodologies are applied to large healthcare datasets, enabling the extraction of significant features, validation of results, and the generation of accurate predictions. The primary purpose of the research is to examine the effectiveness of different models to discover the most robust and reliable technique for predicting diabetes. The focus lies on developing models that can effectively differentiate between diabetic and non-diabetic individuals while achieving high validation scores. By uncovering hidden patterns and trends in the data, the study provides valuable insights for medical professionals, enhancing their ability to make early diagnoses and informed decisions.

articleTitle: An Efficient Switching Scheme for Three Phase Multilevel Voltage Source Solar Inverter using a Novel Spatial Group Improvised Border Collie Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: For three phase multilevel solar inverter, choosing an optimal switching scheme remains a significant challenge. Recently, various new pulse width modulation (PWM)-based switching methods have been efficiently used by the researchers for selecting a novel switching scheme. A novel spatial group improvised border collie optimization (sGIBCO)-based efficient switching scheme has been proposed in this paper to reduce the selective order harmonics. The proposed approach optimally determines the switching angles of the multilevel solar inverter, aiming to minimize the total harmonic distortion (THD). A key innovation of the method lies in its spatial group-based improvisation strategy, where sheep are grouped adaptively based on an calculated distance threshold. An eleven level three phase solar inverter serves as test system for validating the methodology. Comparative analysis with particle swarm optimization (PSO) and harmony search (HS) highlights the superior performance of the proposed sGIBCO technique in optimizing switching schemes. The results indicate that the proposed method can effectively guide the design of hardware multilevel inverters with optimal THD performance.

Author Keywords: spatial group improvised border collie optimization

articleTitle: A Hybrid DWT-SVM Based Approach For Fault Classification in Distribution Systems with Distributed Generators
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Conventional protection relays often struggle to detect shunt faults in distribution systems integrated with Distributed Generators (DGs), including LG, LL, LLG, LLL, and LLLG faults. Existing methods face significant challenges in fault classification and severity diagnosis. This paper introduces a robust fault protection scheme for active distribution systems, leveraging feature extraction using Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) and fault classification using Support Vector Machine (SVM). The proposed method effectively identifies and classifies various fault types, such as symmetrical or asymmetrical faults, addressing the limitations of traditional techniques. The scheme's performance is validated through comprehensive testing on a simulated distribution system using PSCAD software, demonstrating high accuracy and reliability in fault detection and classification. The results highlight the method's potential to enhance fault diagnosis, offering a promising solution for improving protection in modern power systems with complex fault conditions and dynamic operations.

articleTitle: Exploration and Optimization Technique for Speech Enhancement and Emotion Recognition Using Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: One of the most fascinating and difficult tasks in human-computer interaction is speech emotion recognition. The practice of attempting to determine the types of affective and emotional states in speech is known as speech emotion recognition. This takes advantage of the fact that voice pitch and tone often reveal underlying emotion. Animals like horses and dogs also use this phenomenon to understand human emotion. We attempted to identify emotion in a brief voice communication in this experiment. Four datasets–SAVEE, CREMAD, IEMOCAP, TESS, and RAVDESS–that comprise about seven primary emotion types-Happy, Fear, Angry, Disgust, Surprised, Sad, or Neutral-were employed in this effort. In contrast to earlier research, where each researcher worked on a different dataset, our project integrated the four datasets–SAVEE, RAVDESS, TESS, and CREMA-D into a single file, which we then sent as input to the model in the form of a wav file. After removing the noise from the data using feature extraction techniques (MFCC, ZCR, and RMSE), we organized the sequential data in a 3D array format that the CNN model can use. The average accuracy of the model is 76% during the testing phase and 87% during the training phase, according to our repeated testing with different values after putting the data into a graphical format using the Matplotlib tool.

articleTitle: Review of Machine Learning Models for Photonic Crystal
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Photonic crystals (PhCs), with their periodic dielectric structures and unique light-controlling capabilities, are essential in contemporary photonics for applications like waveguides, filters, and resonant cavities. Traditional computational techniques for PhC analysis and design are often time-consuming and demanding. Machine learning (ML) offers efficient and scalable alternatives in this field. This review examines ML models, such as artificial neural networks (ANNs) and generative adversarial networks (GANs), in PhC design and analysis. ANNs forecast optical properties like effective mode area, dispersion relations, and confinement losses, reducing computation time. GANs generate innovative PhC designs and tackle complex optimization challenges. Despite obstacles like overfitting and dataset constraints, these models show potential in streamlining PhC research. This paper explores the methodologies, achievements, and limitations of these ML models, emphasizing their role in advancing photonic device design and optimization. As innovation continues, ML is set to revolutionize PhC research, enabling rapid prototyping and new opportunities in photonics.

articleTitle: An In-Depth Exploration of Different Analog Circuit Parameters Utilizing Three Amplifier Topologies: A Robust Examination of Gain, Power, Noise, and Bandwidth Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: A comparative investigation of transient and AC behaviors of the differential amplifier, cascode operational amplifier, and folded cascode op-amp was performed on Cadence Virtuoso in a 90 nm technology node. The circuits were driven at 1 V with a circuit current of 1 μA. Power consumption, gain, bandwidth, and noise were critically analyzed to compare the performance of these three amplifiers viz. (a) Case-1: differential amplifier, which produced a gain of 10.26 dB, power of 290.4 nW, the noise of 164.1 nV/√Hz, and bandwidth of 23.89 MHz, onwards (b) Case-2: cascode op-amp, that developed gain of 20.59 dB, power of 403.1 nW, noise of 179.6 nV/√Hz, and bandwidth of 1.015 MHz, and ultimately, (c) Case-3: folded cascode op-amp, which generated the aforementioned parameters as 25.02 dB, 684.4 nW, 192.5 nV/√Hz, and 3.822 MHz, respectively. It was found that the folded cascode operational amplifier had a maximum gain. In contrast, the differential amplifier could be operated on a wide range, and the designed differential amplifier was more stable.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Predictive Maintenance for Industrial IoT with Real-Time Fault Detection and Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Predictive maintenance for industrial machinery uses data analysis and advanced techniques to forecast equipment failures. This proactive approach schedules maintenance to minimize downtime and optimize operational efficiency. Achieving accurate, consistent, and well-integrated IoT sensor data is difficult, as poor data quality can result in inaccurate predictions and false alerts. Scaling real-time fault detection and prediction requires substantial computational power and optimized algorithms to process the continuous influx of data from multiple machines. To address data quality and integration issues while enhancing real-time processing and scalability, a Custom Neural Network technique can be used to improve IoT sensor data accuracy and consistency, and efficiently manage the computational demands of continuous data influx for fault detection and prediction. The proposed system, leveraging an extended Neural Network technique, enhances prediction accuracy by efficiently managing diverse industrial datasets and improves real-time fault detection through optimized data processing and reduced latency. The model demonstrated a remarkable accuracy of 92.86%, showcasing its ability to accurately identify both faulty and non-faulty equipment. With a precision of 90.91%, a perfect recall of 100%, and an F1 score of 95.24%, the model exhibited a well-balanced fault detection performance, minimizing false positives while ensuring thorough fault identification, all while processing in real-time with an efficient time complexity of 2.49 seconds.

articleTitle: Sign Language Recognition Using MobileNetV1: A Real Time Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The social significance of recognizing sign language is in the provision of communication means to persons with hearing or speech disorders. In this work, a promising sign language recognition scheme based on the deep learning technique is developed. This system utilizes MobileNetV1 which is a low latency and resource-friendly convolutional neural network architecture modified by transfer learning. For training the model, a 21-class custom sign dataset was used, along with different transformations to the collected sign data. the MobileNetV1 based proposed model yields an accuracy of 97.14 percent on the test set to demonstrate the model capability. Additionally, weighted precision of 0.97, weighted recall of 0.97, and F1 score of 0.97 also supports the ability of the proposed model. Comparative analysis of MobileNetV1 in conjunction with MobileNetV2 and DenseNet establishes the former's effectiveness in high accuracy performance with moderate computational complexity, ideal for real-time usage. Training of the system was carried out by employing various methods including data augmentation and regularization, to develop good generalization and high robustness of the system. This paper also elaborates on new ideas of deep learning models in sign language recognition to real and demanding application into practices for accessibility. This work underlines that the lightweight architectures are crucial to overcome in the conditions of resource limitation and opens the way to the further evolution of the assistive technologies.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Household Equipment Control System Using Laser-LDR Pair
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: To automate several household tasks, it is proposed to have an automation system that combines an arduino uno with a laser and light-dependent resistor (LDR) along with some other sensors. The system detects the entry and exit of a person, senses the internal environment and takes necessary actions. This approach demonstrates a simple yet effective method for automating home functions based on motion detection. The light, temperature and air quality are constantly monitored and corrected to provide a necessary ambiance, that offers convenience, energy savings and enhanced home management.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of an Ultra-Wideband Frequency Selective Surface for 5G Communication Systems and Spatial Filtering Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of an ultra-wideband (UWB) Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) structure tailored for spatial filtering and emerging 5G communication systems. The proposed FSS features a nested square-loop design with a central diamond-shaped patch, achieving excellent frequency selectivity and wide operational bandwidth. The structure offers a reflection coefficient (S21) of less than −10 dB across a bandwidth of 4 GHz to 11 GHz, demonstrating its suitability for UWB applications. Furthermore, it exhibits robust angular stability up to 75° and polarization insensitivity, making it adaptable to real-world scenarios. The simulated surface current distribution and S21 characteristics validate multi- resonance behavior, enabling effective electromagnetic performance for advanced wireless technologies. The proposed design holds significant potential for applications in 5G communication systems, antenna radomes, and electromagnetic shielding, offering a promising solution for next-generation spatial filtering.

articleTitle: Design of a Voltage Controlled Millimeter-Wave Oscillator for 5G/6G Applications in 180nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The paper presents the design of a voltage controlled mm-wave oscillator in 180nm CMOS technology. The oscillator provides a frequency of about 100GHz suitable for 5G/6G applications. The circuit is based on a fourth order LC network giving oscillation for IC realizable component values. Here we have extended the oscillator design by adding the tunability feature to it. This has been accomplished by using PMOS capacitors and changing the capacitance value by controlling the depletion region capacitance through the substrate terminal. The oscillator draws a power of 16.245mW from 1.8V supply and achieves a spot phase noise of - 91.39dBc/Hz @1MHz offset. Such high oscillation frequency and tunability at higher technology node (low cost) has not been seen in the present literature.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an Efficient Quantum Cost Optimized Adder Using Reversible Logic Gates
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: In modern Very-Large-Scale Integration (VLSI) technology, managing information loss is a critical challenge. Conventional logic gates, such as AND, OR, and NOT, are prone to data loss during operations, reducing their efficiency for sophisticated applications. Reversible logic gates, which have an equal number of inputs and outputs, offer a solution by preserving data integrity. This paper presents the design and FPGA implementation of an efficient and high-speed full adder circuit utilizing reversible logic gates, namely Feynman, Toffoli, and Peres gates. The design focuses on improving computational efficiency and thermal performance. An analysis of the circuit's quantum cost, garbage outputs, and ancillary inputs reveals its advantages over traditional designs. Proposed design has been realized using Verilog and Synthesize and simulations performed using Xilinx Vivado and Xilinx ISE tools, confirms the functionality and efficiency of the proposed full adder. FPGA implementation of the design has been done using NEXYS A7 (Artix 7 series). The results show that the circuit has a quantum cost of 10, with two garbage outputs and one ancillary input, underscoring its potential for use in low-power, high-performance computing systems and quantum computing applications.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Intelligent Real-Time ATM Monitoring and Alert System to Enhance Security
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The Face Mask Detection and Alert System for ATM security enhancement is a cutting-edge technology designed to improve safety and preserve the integrity of ATM facilities. The technology uses deep learning and computer vision to identify people with concealed facial features, such as those who wear masks, helmets or purposefully cover their faces. The research uses a pretrained Convolutional Neural network to analyze real-time video streams, recognizing and classifying faces based on mask compliance. When a violation is identified, the system sends out an automated notice that includes an audible alarm, a photo of the individual, and an email message to authorities with the taken image attached. This ingenious system not only enhances ATM security but also serves as a deterrent to unwanted activity. Its real-time monitoring capabilities are actionable. Alerts provide a proactive solution to today's security challenges. The system, built for efficiency, scalability, and user-friendliness, demonstrates machine learning's potential to address critical safety concerns.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Low Power Low Phase Noise Pseudoresistive Astable Multivibrator for MICS Band Wireless Sensor Node Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The paper presents the design of an ultra-low power pseudoresistive astable multivibrator for Medical Implant Communications Service (MICS) band applications. Instead of tail current source, we have used a MOSFET operating in deep triode region (acting as pseudoresistor) which reduces the 1/f3 noise corner of the phase noise spectrum. Complementary MOSFETs have been used as switches for linearization of its output resistance which reduces the phase noise further. A resistor based tuning circuit provides bias to the pseudoresistor which can be used for changing the frequency. The outputs are pseudodifferential (accomplished by two cross-coupled low strength CMOS inverters) providing rejection to common-mode noise. The entire circuit has been designed and simulated in Cadence Virtuoso using gpdk180 nm technology library and draws a current of 150µA from 1.8V power supply while achieving a phase noise of −100dBc/Hz @ 1 MHz offset. Such low phase noise performance at this ultra-low power has not been seen in other MICS band oscillators so far.

articleTitle: A Review on the Minimization of Energy Consumption in Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Blockchain is considered one of the most innovative technologies and applied across various fields with applications in, for example, education, business, and many more. First introduced as the technology that underlies Bitcoin, blockchain has since evolved to an important means of safekeeping digital information without involving intermediaries. With growing popularity among businesses, there are rising concerns about environmental impacts, particularly energy usage. Blockchain is known for extremely high energy consumption because of the agreement methodologies applied, specifically Proof of Work(PoW). The paper addresses blockchain technology, namely the various algorithms generated and their influence on the environment. It also looks into emerging concepts and strategies in reducing the energy impact of blockchain technology, including moving to Proof of Stake (PoS), hybrid consensus approaches, and exploiting renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: RAIL: Recursive A* and Imitation Learning-Based Approach for Collision-Free Path Estimation
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This paper discusses collision-free path planning for autonomous vehicles, a crucial aspect of their development. The authors propose a method to detect objects of different sizes, both dynamic and static, and compare algorithms for path planning and avoidance of collision. They use traditional path-finding algorithms like A* Algorithm, which include heuristics and Rapidly Exploring Random Tree (RRT) algorithms for real-time analysis. The authors discuss the challenges of ensuring path-planning algorithms scale to large environments and operate in real-time, and the need for future work on improving the robustness of path-planning algorithms in dynamic and unpredictable scenarios. The methodology involves creating a dataset, analyzing images, and training neural networks to imitate the collision-free path- finding algorithm. Static obstacles change their coordinates with time, making working in dynamic environments difficult. Recursive A* and Imitation Learning (RAIL) based approaches analyze obstacles frame by frame, making them static at a particular time-instant. The Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) and Inverse Reinforcement Learning are used to train an imitation learning model for faster trajectory finding in autonomous vehicles. Future development could involve using the Internet of Things (IoT) to share the trained trajectory-finding model results.

articleTitle: Secured Visible Light Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The development of advanced Visible Light Communication (VLC) system has opened the gates for very high speed and extremely secure data exchange. With the need for a transmission method which can resist transmission interference, this technology utilizes the hidden potential of the visible light spectrum. The system includes a highly precise red laser optimized with a help of a biconvex lens set on both transmitting and receiving ends for duplex messaging. It is made further secure by using simple encryption methods to protect data. Experimental results show that this system is much better than the one using radio frequency in terms of performance, specifically in sensitive environments such as in military sites or for medical purposes. It can be implemented on any existing light setup hence making it easy to access & cost effective. This solution can be further advanced by using machine learning to improve performance, while stronger security methods and advanced technologies like MIMO (Multiple Input Multiple Output) are some of the prospects in future Optical Wireless Network (OWN).

articleTitle: Algorithmic Approach to Controlled Deforestation: An Optimized Model for Ecological and Economic Outcomes
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: In an era where rapid urbanization and environmental degradation often clash, balancing development with ecological preservation has become a critical challenge. This work presents a practical framework for optimizing decisions around deforestation, with afforestation serving as a vital complement to maintain ecological stability. The model uses straightforward algorithms and real-time data to evaluate the connections between tree cover, air quality, and pollution levels. By analyzing spatial data on plant species distributions and pollution trends, the framework employs clustering techniques like DBSCAN and decision-making methods such as AHP and TOPSIS to identify deforestation zones that would minimize environmental harm. Results show a significant improvement in air quality with selected regions experiencing a 31.1% increase in AQI compared to the average. Additionally, the framework highlights the importance of afforestation in restoring lost tree cover and reducing the long-term ecological impact of deforestation. By harnessing real-time data and insights on tree species and their distribution, this model offers a clear pathway toward cleaner air, healthier ecosystems, and sustainable development. This approach offers actionable insights into sustainable land management.

articleTitle: Real-Time Sentiment Analysis of Comments and Reviews: A Kafka Driven Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Buyers make desired decisions based on reviews available on E-commerce platforms (i.e., the ratings and an overview of pertinent item text are used for decision making). E-commerce giants like Amazon and Flipkart provide a platform that allows customers to share their experiences, offering real insights about product performance to future buyers. People trust reviews, and Amazon customers often check online reviews before purchasing a product. A high number of reviews suggests that a product is popular, while numerous positive reviews may indicate its high quality. To extract valuable insights from an extensive collection of reviews, grouping reviews into positive and negative sentiments is necessary. Sentiment Analysis, the process of detecting positive or negative sentiments in text, is commonly used by businesses to assess social data, gauge brand reputation, and understand customers. To enhance the existing sentiment analysis, a real-time sentiment analysis pipeline will be introduced using Message Queues as the backbone for event-driven processing. Instead of batch processing reviews, the new system will stream customer reviews in real time, allowing for near-instant classification and analysis. This will involve multiple steps: Real-time data ingestion from various sources (e-commerce platforms, social media) using Kafka producers. Stream processing, Trend Monitoring, Scalability and fault tolerance enabled by Kafka, ensuring the system can handle high data throughput from diverse sources.

articleTitle: Composing the Future: Music Generation with Recurrent Neural Networks for Creative Empowerment
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The emergence of neural networks (RNNs) for music generation is changing the landscape of content creation, especially on platforms like YouTube, where artists' shows and producers support AI-generated music. This paper explores the process of using RNNs to generate music, focusing on an in-depth experiment that demonstrates the design, training, and implementation of the technology. RNNs reduce the complexity of music production by simplifying the mixing process and making music accessible to a wide range of creators, including those without a musical background. Our research examines the fundamentals of RNN-based music production in detail and demonstrates its potential to support innovation and independent content production. Through this experiment, we open up new possibilities in AI-driven creativity by demonstrating how RNNs can be effectively used to create both beautiful and noisy music.

articleTitle: Interpretable AI for Alzheimer's Diagnosis Using Cross-Sectional and Longitudinal Data
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder causing severe cognitive decline, particularly in older adults. Early diagnosis is crucial for effective treatment, yet traditional methods rely on costly neuroimaging techniques like MRI, limiting accessibility for lower-income groups. This paper proposes an affordable, interpretable machine learning framework for AD diagnosis using only cross-sectional and longitudinal clinical data. The model classifies patients into non-demented, mild, moderate, and severe dementia stages by leveraging temporal features such as MMSE score variations and brain volume changes over time. Explainable AI techniques enhance transparency, making the model clinically relevant and trustworthy. Experimental results show high classification accuracy, with LightGBM outperforming other models. By prioritizing clinical data over expensive imaging, this approach offers a scalable and costeffective diagnostic solution. The study underscores the role of interpretable AI in improving AD diagnosis and facilitating integration into real-world clinical settings.

articleTitle: Utilization of Response Surface Methodology to Optimize the Banana/Carbon with Nanoparticle Parameters in Mechanical Properties
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The research focuses on the effects of varying Nano-graphene fillers on the tensile and flexural strengths of composites made from a blend of natural resource banana fiber and carbon fibers. The specific Nano-graphene filler tested were 1wt %, 2 wt %, 3 wt%. The researchers used Response Surface Methodology (RSM) with Central Composite Designs (CCD) to structure and evaluate their experiments, with a focus on identifying the optimal settings for the Nanofiller, as well as the proportions of banana and carbon fibers. This approach allowed them to create quadratic models to predict the tensile and flexural strengths of the composites. Through comprehensive experiments, the researchers determined that the ideal configuration for achieving the highest tensile strength (T) involved a 3 wt% of nanofiller and fiber content of 40 percent for both banana and carbon fibers. Under these conditions, the tensile strength increased by 30.79% and the flexural strength (F) by 21.47% compared to the data derived from RSM. These significant improvements indicate that varying the nanofiller can effectively boost the tensile and bending strengths, enhancing the bond between natural fibers and matrix.

articleTitle: Secure Ultra Wideband FSS Structure for Spatial Filter and Upcoming 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Ultra-wideband (UWB) radio technology is frequently employed for high-bandwidth, short-range applications. across a broad range of the radio spectrum. UWB typically operates over a range of frequencies between 3.1 GHz and 10.6 GHz making it well-suited for various high-speed communication and precise localization applications. The generation of UWB occurs due to generation of radio energy at specific time intervals and through this it possess larger bandwidth thereby enabling pulse position or time modulation. This project describes a low profile of polarization insensitive and angularly stable frequency selective surface (FSS) has been achieved with a rejection band from 5.432GHz to 20.264GHz at 10 dB insertion loss. This proposed design is applicable for possible Wi-Fi applications and it can also work as a functional EM shield for 5G network applications.

articleTitle: Efficient Power Management for Always on Display (AOD) Feature with 2.5D Graphics on Wearables : A Low-Power Design Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Wearable technology is seen as one of the advance paradigm in various applications such as fitness, health care, etc. Smartwatches are engineered to integrate seamlessly into modern lifestyles, designed to enhance productivity, health and connectivity. The popularity of smartwatches has been steadily increasing due to various factors such as growing technology adoption, tech-savvy youth, health and fitness focus, etc. but one of the key challenges facing smartwatches is battery life. Lower battery life can be inconvenient for many users who rely heavily on their smartwatches throughout the day for various functions. The display stands out as a primary power-consuming component in a smartwatch. Furthermore, the implementation of features like always-on display can exacerbate battery drainage. These posed challenges in meeting the required battery life to improve overall user experience and satisfaction. We propose a novel approach to enhance battery life through efficient power management using 2.5D graphics. We present novel solution for wearable devices to provide low powered display solutions with 2.5D graphics. To prove the validity of our solution, we show experimental results using 2.5D graphics on smartwatch. Details of our proposed solution for efficient power management on wearables are presented.

articleTitle: SafeGuard Bangle: A Smart Wearable with Emergency Panic Button for Women's Safety
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Women's safety is a significant global topic, needing novel technical solutions, which can be easy to use and daily wearable. This paper proposes the SafeGuard Bangle, a wearable smart gadget prototype that has an emergency panic button and GPS features to improve women's security. Using important components such as the Neo-6M GPS module, WeMos D1 Mini microcontroller, TP4056 charging module, and an SOS button, the gadget provides real-time location tracking and alerts. This prototype works with the Blynk app to allow smooth connectivity and fast communication in an emergency, it uses satellite to track down the exact location and provide the coordinates for the same. By addressing the crucial need for women's safety, this technology provides consumers with a portable, dependable, and effective solution. Its cost-effectiveness and durable design make it a key leap in wearable technology for personal security. This solution is made for every class of women whether she is living in rural or urban area.

articleTitle: A Mathematical Model to Study the Effect of Porous Parameter on Blood Flow Through an Atherosclerotic Arterial Segment Having Slip Velocity
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Circulatory disorders, including atherosclerosis and arterial stenosis, are major causes of morbidity and mortality, leading to critical conditions like ischemia and heart attacks. Arteries narrow due to abnormal deposits of cholesterol and fats, increasing blood flow resistance and altering shear stress distribution. A systematic study of blood flow behaviour in diseased arteries is vital for better understanding, diagnosis, and treatment of cardiovascular conditions. Blood being a suspension of fats and cholesterols in aquatic plasma, exhibits non- Newtonian behaviour, particularly at low shear rates, necessitating specialized models for accurate flow analysis. This research presents a mathematical model to study the effect of porous parameters and slip velocity on blood flow through a stenosed diseased arterial segment. The model uses the Herschel-Bulkley fluid model for non Newtonian blood flow and Darcy's law to describe flow through porous arterial walls. The geometry of stenosis is modelled as a symmetric, radially constricted section of the artery. Key parameters include stenosis height, length, and position. Numerical computations are performed to analyse flow resistance and wall shear stress. Results demonstrate that increased porous parameters and stenosis severity raises the flow resistance and wall shear stress, while incorporating slip velocity reduces these effects. These highlight the significance of velocity slip and porous properties in refining flow models. In conclusion, integrating porous media characteristics and slip velocity improves blood flow analysis, offering more accurate insights into stenosis-induced hemodynamic changes. This study provides a foundation for future research aimed at optimizing therapeutic strategies for managing cardiovascular diseases.

articleTitle: RISC-V: Redefining the Future of Computing, Architecture, Innovations, and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: In recent years, RISC-V has gained significant popularity and RISC-V computing device is going to increase by 2030 due to open-source and royalty-free instruction set architecture (ISA). RISC-V is widely adopted as an ISA for embedded processors globally. India has launched the Digital India RISC-V (DIR-V) program for next generation microprocessors in 2022, and many organizations have started working on the RISC-VISA. The RISC-V standards organization consistently introduces new ISA extensions to cater to the evolving requirements of advanced computing. The widespread of use of Android/Wear OS is attributed to technological advancements and the availability of cost-effective solutions for mobile and wearable devices. There are many operating systems are available for embedded devices such as iOS, Android, Tizen and FireFox. Among all of these OS Android is one of the most popular OS for wide variety of devices such as smartphones, wearable, automotive, smart TV, etc. In this paper, we present the study of RISC vs RISC-V. Further, the details of challenges to run operating system especially linux kernel based OS on RISC-V is covered.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Approach for Predicting Personality Types from Text Patterns Using Natural Language Processing(NLP)
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This study explores the use of Natural Language Processing (NLP) approach to predict Myers-Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI) personality types from Twitter texts. Initially, we approached the problem as a 16-class classification task, but encountered significant challenges due to the lack of instances representing certain class labels adequately. To address this, we decomposed the MBTI types into four dimensions and trained individual classifiers for each dimension. Leveraging the best performing classifiers, we constructed a stacking ensemble model to predict personality classes corresponding to each dimension. The results demonstrate improved accuracy compared to the initial 16-class classification approach. Additionally, the performance of ensemble model is found to be better than the individual classifiers. Thus, ensemble approach paired with the separate dimension based classification method can be used for effective prediction of personality types for psychological profiling.

articleTitle: A Brief Review on Smart Farming Technologies for Precision Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Farming sustains the global population, currently over 7.9 billion people. As the population continues to grow, the importance of farming becomes even more critical. This review explores the latest advancements in smart farming technologies and their application in precision agriculture. Smart farming integrates cutting-edge technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), and big data analytics to enhance agricultural productivity and sustainability. By leveraging these technologies, precision agriculture aims to optimize resource use, reduce environmental impact, and increase crop yields. Various research groups are working on these cutting-edge technologies which is briefly reviewed and discussed here.

articleTitle: Simulation-Based Optimization of Battery and Motor Configurations for Enhanced Efficiency and Sustainability in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The transition to electric and hybrid vehicles is critical for achieving global sustainability goals and reducing environmental impact. This paper presents a simulation-based methodology for optimizing battery and motor selection in hybrid electric vehicle (HEV) systems, focusing on key performance metrics such as energy efficiency, range, costeffectiveness, and reliability. By systematically evaluating various battery and motor configurations, the study demonstrates significant improvements in energy consumption, extended driving range, and system durability. The model is created in MATLAB Simulink environment and examined under various circuit conditions.

articleTitle: Spiral Ring Resonator-Based Dual-Band Waveguide BPF for Satellite CDMA Signal Tracking in a 5G Environment
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band waveguide band pass filter is designed and simulated at the C-band. First, short lines are formed between the vertical wall along the width, and each line has two spiral ring resonators attached at the midpoints on either side. These spiral resonators are resonating at frequencies of 3411 and 4190 MHz. To obtain appropriate band pass responses, the number of turns in the spiral is increased from one to two, and two metallic solid slabs are introduced between the two symmetrical short lines with spiral ring resonators, all of which are enclosed within a metallic cavity measuring <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$40\times 30\times 30 \text{mm}^{3}$</tex>. The simulation results demonstrate a dual-band band pass filter with bandwidths of 2900–2978 MHz and 3788–3860 MHz. The insertion loss in the first band is -1 dB and -0.12 dB in the second band. A very sharp band is also coming at the 3500 MHz frequency, which is undesirable. The proposed filter architecture should make the station work better, making it easier to track and get satellite CDMA signals in the complicated 5G RF environment that is full of interference.

articleTitle: An Efficient Digital Vedic Multiplier with an Enhanced Adder
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)

authors.preferredName: Surya V. N. S. V. Chakka

abstract: Multipliers are key components in digital signal processors, where there is a high demand for high-speed hardware. The multiplier's performance is typically assessed using three main factors: speed, power and area. The new Vedic Multiplier uses a Speed Efficient Carry Select Adder (CSA) to improve the speed and also consume less power in the multiplication process. The Crosswise and Vertical Multiplication algorithm breaks down the input values into smaller segments, which are then multiplied by using the algorithm to produce partial output. The conclusive result is generated by adding these partial outputs with the help of CSA. In this project, a 16-bit Vedic Multiplier is created using Verilog HDL by incorporating CSA, half adders and full adders. The simulation is done using ModelSim and the design is synthesized using Cadence Genus. The proposed methodology has reduced delay by 8.6% and also reduced power consumption by 24.55% results compared to conventional CSA.

articleTitle: A Strategic Framework for the Development of a Microtext AI Chatbot for Tourism in Indian Cities
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Tourism plays a crucial role in India's economy, with its diverse cultural, historical, and geographical richness attracting millions of domes-tic and international visitors annually. To cater to the needs of these travelers and enhance their overall experience, there is a growing need for inno-vative technological solutions. This paper presents a comprehensive literature survey, analyzing existing research, trends, and practical implementations of microtext normalization as well as the application of chatbots in the context of tourism. Furthermore, it proposes a strategic framework for the development and deployment of an effective microtext AI chatbot tailored to the requirements of tourism in India. The proposed design leverages modern machine learning and natural language processing (NLP) strategies for providing personalized, context-aware assistance to tourists in order to enhance their overall experience while exploring the various cities of India.

articleTitle: Star Fruit Maturity Detection for the Comparative Study Between RGB and L*A*B* Image Processing Methods
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Assessing fruit quality is crucial for cultivators and consumers. The present study introduces an image processing method to determine the maturity of starfruit by comparing L*A*B* and RGB color spaces. High-resolution images were taken using smartphone's camera (50 Mega Pixel with Sony IMX766 sensor), and a MATLAB (R2024b) tool to analyze fruit maturity and ripeness. Ripening and color change in fruits is closely related, as shifts in pigment concentrations affect their appearance over time, and analyzing the color change, the ripeness of starfruit can be accurately assessed. The study emphasizes the effect of different color space on the analysis of the results, and demonstrate that image processing is a reliable way to classify fruit maturity. These results support better quality control in fruit processing facilities and enhance production efficiency.

articleTitle: Importance of Design in Web Accessibility: A Result Based Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: With an emphasis on user-centred design, this study examines the potential and difficulties of enhancing web accessi-bility for those with impairments. The paper reviews the existing literature on web accessibility and user-centered design and presents an analysis of a group of websites where user-centered design principles can be incorporated to improve accessibility for the people with cognitive impairments and visually impaired. The case study indicates that user-centered design can significantly improve web accessibility, by providing interfaces and content that are tailored to the needs and preferences of users with disabilities. The research paper concludes with requirement of more holistic and inclusive approach to web design which will make the web pages for all users, including those specially-ablaed. The findings of this research have practical implications for designers, developers and stakeholders who are working to make the internet accessible to all and contribute to the growing knowledge on web accessibility.

articleTitle: Predicting Chronic Kidney Disease Using Machine Learning Methodologies
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) harms the kidneys and affects their ability to eliminate waste and preserve the balance of body fluids. Complications include abnormal bones, poor nutrition, neurological problems, anemia (low red blood cell count), high blood pressure, and acid-base imbalances. Early and precise detection of CKD is essential to stop further deterioration in health. Reliable prediction algorithms are necessary to improve early detection and management due to its high propensity to progress into end-stage renal disease. The goal of this study is to improve CKD prediction using machine learning (ML) methods. This method employs sophisticated techniques such as Random Forest, k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Gradient Boosting, Naive Bayes, CatBoost, and AdaBoost. The proposed work determines the most effective ML methods for early prediction in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. We have considered the UCI repository datasets for simulation purposes, which contain 400 entries and 24 attributes. It was examined using different ML methods to identify the most effective predictive models for the early detection and better treatment of individuals affected by CKD. The random forest (RF), gradient boosting (GB), Adaboost (AdaB), CatBoost (CatB) models achieve the highest overall performance, with an accuracy of 100% and the navie bayes (NB), and KNN approaching 97%, the findings demonstrated remarkable precision. This study demonstrates how ML can improve the early detection of CKD and promote more effective healthcare practices.

articleTitle: Smart Playground for Electricity Generation Using Swing
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The world's energy demand is rapidly increasing due to rise in population. Energy generation is mainly dependent on fossil fuels, nuclear energy and renewable energy resources. Therefore, there is a need for a cleaner method to generate electricity which can act as a substitute for the existing methods. This paper proposes an innovative method of generating electricity using play equipment like swings. The motion of the swing has been used in the present work to move the shaft back and forth which will drive the sprockets and transfer the momentum to the spur gear arrangement. This runs the dynamo and generates electricity, and it can then be stored in batteries or kinetic energy storing equipment and then used later. The proposed method minimizes environmental impact, reduces energy consumption and promotes sustainability.

articleTitle: FPGA-Based Adaptive Traffic Management System for Optimizing Five-Point Intersection Flow
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The present invention relates to an FPGA driven traffic management system specifically designed for five-point intersections, which are notably complex due to their unique traffic flow patterns. FPGA is field programmable gate of array basically used to implement digital virtual logic into real hardware. Here FPGAs are utilized to process and control this system periodically every 360 sec durations. This innovative approach not only improves traffic flow and reduces waiting times but also contributes to handle emergency like situation and according to that manipulate signals. The adaptability of the invention to diverse traffic conditions makes it a robust solution for urban traffic management challenges.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of PSO, ACO and Hybrid ACO-PSO for Multi-Target Search Using Autonomous Swarm Drones in Obstacle-Rich Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: In this paper, we present a performance comparison of the algorithms of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), and the hybrid ACO-PSO algorithms in performing multi-target search with drones in environments cluttered with obstacles. This is evaluated along the aspects of path quality, search efficiency, execution time, and how obstacles are handled. In our simulation, we performed the initial search with both ACO and PSO in isolation, followed by the hybrid ACO-PSO approach. Our results suggest that the hybrid ACO-PSO algorithm outperforms the stand-alone methods because of its enhanced adaptability, as it well balances exploration and exploitation and also avoids the problem of local optima.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Circular Microstrip Patch Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a 5G reconfigurable microstrip patch antenna, capable of operating in multiple 5G frequency bands. Three design scenarios are investigated, including a single radiating patch, a dual radiating patch, and a switch connecting both patches. The switch enables the antenna to reconfigure and operate in two different 5G frequency bands, covering the n77 band (3.3-4.2 GHz) and (3.1-3.85 GHz). The simulated results show that the antenna achieves a resonant bandwidth of 4.04 GHz and 4.05 GHz for the single and dual patch designs, respectively, and 3.26 GHz and 3.56 GHz for the RLC switch-enabled design. The proposed antenna design offers a promising solution for 5G applications requiring frequency reconfigurability and compact size.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Filter Responses of Bandpass Filter for Sub-6 Band Application
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This study provides a detailed comparison of five popular bandpass filter responses: Bessel, Butterworth, Chebyshev-I, Chebyshev-II, and Elliptical. This paper explains the concepts for designing each filter type along with circuit diagrams. The filters are designed for the frequency range of 3.3 GHz to 3.8 GHz, commonly known as the sub-6 band, which is frequently used in 5G communication systems. The frequency responses of each filter are compared in order to do the comparative study of insertion loss, bandwidths, cut-offs, and passband shape. The study intends to provide a full review of these filters' performance in the sub-6 GHz band, helping engineers and researchers in selecting the most effective filter type for their requirements.

articleTitle: Optimizing Diabetic Kidney Disease Diagnosis with Machine Learning: A Novel Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a diabetic condition in which elevated blood sugar levels harm the kidney's filtering units, leading to kidney damage and potentially, kidney failure. About 700 million people effected by Diabetic Kidney Disease of whom approximately four million patients require kidney replacement therapy (KRT). The existing methods for predicting Diabetic Kidney Disease (DKD) have several drawbacks that limit their effectiveness and accuracy. Current models often rely on traditional biomarkers, such as blood glucose and urine albumin levels, which can be insufficient for early detection as they typically indicate kidney damage only after it has progressed. Proposed a novel technique by utilizing machine learning algorithm such as navie Bayes to predict the DKD in early stage leads to decrease the mortality rate. Proposed invention enhances the accuracy in disease diagnosis, which result in the score of 96.03, 94.03, 95.08 and 95.09 with precision, accuracy recall and F1-Score respectively.

articleTitle: IOT-Based Home Automation for LPG Gas and Fire Detection System With Automated Safety Measures
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This paper introduces an advanced IoT-driven system aimed at identifying LPG gas leaks and fire hazards while providing automated safety mechanisms and real-time monitoring the mq2 sensor is utilized for detecting variations in gas concentrations and the DHT11 sensor monitors temperature fluctuations to identify potential fire risks an Arduino UNO serves as the core controller processing data from the sensors and initiating safety responses such as triggering an audible alarm rotating a servo motor to shut off the gas supply and powering an exhaust fan to vent the leaked gas to enable remote oversight the ESP32 module communicates with the Arduino and transmits data to the Blynk IoT platform allowing users to monitor conditions in real-time additionally the system integrates GSM-based functionality to deliver alerts via SMS or calls complementing app notifications and emails this comprehensive design ensures rapid response to emergencies offering a reliable and practical safety solution for environments vulnerable to gas leaks and fire outbreaks.

articleTitle: Framework for Edu-Metaverse: Integrating Immersive Technologies for Collaborative and Experimental Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The convergence of education and technology has paved the way for transformative innovations, with the Metaverse and immersive experiences offering unprecedented opportunities for interactive learning. However, a significant gap persists in the development of educational applications-namely, the absence of a robust framework for seamlessly integrating these technologies into educational ecosystems. To address this, we propose an innovative approach that incorporates artificial intelligence through a 3D chatbot, designed to act as an interactive guide for students. This chatbot not only answers questions but also delivers supplementary learning resources, fostering a more engaging learning experience. Additionally, our framework integrates live streaming and chat functionalities, enabling realtime communication between students and educators, regardless of geographic location. By bridging these technological gaps, our solution aims to enhance traditional educational environments, significantly improving engagement and accessibility for learners worldwide.
