This initiative represents a critical step toward a future where education is both highly interactive and profoundly impactful. This is an exciting step towards creating a future where learning is not just informative, but genuinely engaging and impactful.

articleTitle: Non-Invasive Junction Temperature Measurement Using Forward Voltage Drop of High-Power pcLED Under Tropical Conditions
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: High Power White pcLEDs have revolutionized lighting technology, replacing conventional electrical lighting. Their useful life depends on factors like junction temperature, which is crucial for thermal management. Measurement of junction temperature is essential for estimating device reliability and useful life. However, it is not directly measurable due to its non-accessibility. Instead, indirect techniques like measuring the solder point and using thermal models are used. A better technique is using the p-n junction as a sensor, calibrating the forward voltage drop across the junction at various temperatures. This non-invasive technique offers a simple, accurate, and precise method for determining junction temperature in semiconductor p-n junctions. This method provides a rough estimate of the LED's useful life, as junction temperature is a major factor in determining its lifetime. This non-invasive technique has potential industrial scale advantages.

articleTitle: A Fast Sampling-Based Synchronization Technique for Single-Phase Grid Connected Inverter
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Phase-Lock-Loop (PLL) is one of the most challenging aspects in Grid Connected Inverter (GCI) applications, as the synchronization must be done between the inverter output and the grid for a controlled operation. Most PLLs are based on the optimization between performance and complexity. A highly complex PLL technique, having the ability to perform accurately even in distorted grid conditions, has no additional use in household or low-cost applications. Most household appliances are rated only for standard grid conditions, and a complex PLL method often compromises with cost and reliability. The author of this paper strongly believes that a cheap but reliable PLL technique is more preferable to large-scale consumers, compared to an expensive and complex PLL technique. In this paper, a fast sampling-based PLL technique using some basic arithmetic operations, some basic modules, and some peripheral registers has been proposed and implemented through a DSP microcontroller. This technique significantly reduces the computational burden, so less processing time helps to achieve fast and accurate responses.

articleTitle: Development Of AI Based Solar Water Pump For Agricultural Application
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: In this paper, the solar-powered water pumping system performance that makes use of a switching reluctance motor (SRM) drive is analyzed with two-stage proposed system. In the first stage, a new structure of DC-DC SEPIC (Single-ended Primary Inductance Converter) is used and in the second stage, a Switching Reluctance Motor is powered by using an asymmetric bridge converter. Artificial Neural Network (ANN) was utilized for the maximum power point (MPP) tracking of Solar PV and used for the SEPIC converter's duty ratio control. The control of SRM is achieved using closed-loop control, having feedback signals of current & speed. The high-voltage solar panel arraying complexity is eliminated by the modified converter, and it also addresses the panel hotspot issues. MATLAB/Simulink is used for design and testing the developed system in standard environmental testing conditions and results have been observed to be satisfactory.

articleTitle: Design of Frequency Reconfigurable Antenna for C-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: In this paper, a frequency-reconfigurable antenna for C-band applications is designed. The antenna consists of four curved dipoles on both sides of the substrate. It is excited with the help of the coaxial feed from the center. The bandwidth, gain, S parameter (return loss), and VSWR of the antenna have been analyzed. For frequency reconfiguration, varactor diodes are incorporated. The center frequency of the antenna can be tuned from 4.58- 4.755 GHz. The ratio of the tuning range to the original bandwidth of the antenna (RBW) is 92%, which indicates an improvement of 12%. The antenna is designed and simulated using Ansys HFSS software.

articleTitle: Integrating Battery Energy Storage Systems for Enhanced Grid Reliability and Renewable Energy Management
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: India's renewable energy capacity reached 120 GW in 2023, driven by solar and wind growth. To stabilize the grid and enhance energy reliability, Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) are crucial. This project investigates BESS integration into the Indian power grid using MATLAB and Simulink. Batteries emerged as the most feasible solution due to declining costs (84% fall since 2010) and technological advancements. Simulations will model BESS under various scenarios. This project aims to demonstrate that integrating BESS can enhance grid reliability and flexibility while offering a financially viable solution for renewable energy management in India.

articleTitle: FPGA-Based 3D EM/MPM Simulation Framework for Medical Image Segmentation Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Medical image segmentation is a critical process in identifying disease-infected regions for diagnostic and treatment purposes. This paper introduces an FPGA-based framework for implementing the Expectation Maximization/Markov Random Field (E M/MP M) algorithm in 3D medical image segmentation. FPGA platforms offer unparalleled advantages in terms of parallel processing, speed, and energy efficiency, making them a promising choice for real-time medical image analysis. This proposed framework enables rapid segmentation of 3D images, leveraging the FPGA's on-chip memory and custom logic for efficient pixel classification and data processing. The adaptive design also supports the integration of external RAM for larger datasets. Simulated using Verilog HDL and Quartus Prime, this work demonstrates accurate segmentation results through virtual testing, thus showcasing the system's robustness for medical applications.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Efficacy of Text Summarization Models: A Comparison of NLP Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Text Summarization is a critical tool nowadays. People do not have enough time to read big articles which take a lot of time. A short summary is no doubt an enthralling option for this case. As this demand increases numerous algorithms and methods have come up which can serve this purpose. This survey paper encompasses the different algorithms and methods used by different researchers which includes methods like TF-IDF and LSA alongside neural networks like Seq2Seq, Pegasus, and Transformer-based models like BART and T5. We analyze these on metrics like ROUGE scores. This survey paper will provide a valuable resource for researchers in the future who want to study text summarization in the news domain.

articleTitle: Integrating AI and IoT for Smarter Decision Support in Entrepreneurial Ecosystems
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This paper looks at the applicability of AI and IoT in promoting Technology Business Incubators to improve entrepreneurial environments. TBIs are essential for giving access to new and fundamental resources such as mentorship, networking and infrastructure for entrepreneurs. However, many fail to allocate resources and manage operations and stakeholder's relations efficiently. This research aims to make an improved recommendation of AI for predictive analysis and IoT for real-time analysis to improve management decisions and optimise resource utilisation for better startup performance. Following a multi-method approach, the work employs descriptive analysis, correlation studies, and lastly regression modeling on varied data sets. The results presented in the work highlight high accuracy of the proposed framework for predicting the success of startups and an informative approach to the management of resources for improving the decision-making process. The suggested framework can be implemented as best practice for TBIs since it addresses the management and steering challenges, focuses on resource efficiency, and supports incubator managers and policymakers in establishing sustainable environments for entrepreneurship.

articleTitle: A Review on Fault Localization Techniques in Transmission and Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The efficient transmission of electrical energy in bulk requires a highly reliable transmission system. Fault identification is, therefore, a critical aspect of power distribution networks. Fault detection and localization are essential tasks for engineers, as they facilitate fault clearance and the maintenance of transmission lines, underground cables, and even hybrid power transmission systems. Various methods are employed for fault localization, each with its own strengths and weaknesses. This review paper provides a comprehensive survey of these methods, highlighting their advantages, limitations, and effectiveness in different scenarios.

articleTitle: Robust Frequency Regulation of Power System Through Aggregated Variable Speed Air-Conditioner Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Frequency regulation services through demand-side measures such as thermostatically controlled loads have gained popularity in the recent decade. However, there is a significant need for a control strategy that has the capability to provide regulation even under parametric uncertainties. In this paper, a robust PI controller has been designed to homogeneously integrate aggregated Variable Speed Air-Conditioning (VSAC) systems into a Single-Area Power System (SAPS) with a reheat steam turbine. Based on parametric uncertainties, a worst-case model of the VSAC-SAPS system is obtained and its stability margins in terms of Phase and Gain margins are evaluated. Simulation results show that the dynamic responses of the power grid's frequency and power deviation of the grid were steady-state stable. Considering 30,000 homogeneous VSACs with 1.5 tonnes capacity, the rated power of the aggregated VSACs is 59MW (approx.). Simulation results showed that without a robust controller, the uncertain system was stable but sensitive to perturbations due to lower gain and phase margins. Frequency support services were utilized from the grid and aggregated VSAC systems, thereby significantly reducing the strain on the conventional grid. The robust PI controller in the VSAC system enhances transient stability by reducing overshoot and achieving faster damping, complementing the slower grid response.

articleTitle: Empowering Women's Safety: Artificial Intelligence and IoT-Enabled Smart Wearable Device for Real-Time Monitoring and Emergency Assistance
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Women's safety remains a pressing concern worldwide, necessitating multifaceted approaches to address physical, emotional, and social threats. Despite strides in gender equality, women still face significant risks of violence and harassment in diverse settings, from homes and workplaces to public spaces. It is estimated that globally, 137 women are killed each day by an intimate partner or a family member. Furthermore, in the United States, 19.3% of women have experienced rape at some point in their lives, and 43.9% have been subjected to sexual violence other than rape. Technological innovations, like safety apps and improved public transport security, offer additional protective layers. Many safety apps and devices are inaccessible due to cost, lack of awareness, or technological literacy, particularly in underprivileged or rural areas. Our aim is to create a system that will help make every location and every minute safer for women. The goal of this invention is to design an Android app that women may use in any type of scenario in day-to-day life. The proposed Android-based application will subsequently update the user's position from dawn to evening. When an individual crosses the geographical region, an SMS alert is delivered to the selected contact already updated in the mobile app and also send an alert when the user vital signs exceeds threshold values.

articleTitle: MCU-Enhanced Underwater Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Underwater image dehazing is a critical challenge due to light absorption, scattering, and color degradation. This paper presents a comprehensive dehazing methodology combining physical modeling and image enhancement techniques. The approach begins by computing the dark channel to estimate transmission and atmospheric light, enabling accurate haze removal. A multi-scale guided filter refines the transmission map, enhancing edge preservation. Scene radiance is then recovered, followed by brightness adjustment and contrast enhancement using CLAHE in the LAB color space. To further enhance visual clarity, the method applies unsharp masking for sharpening. This pipeline effectively addresses underwater image degradation, producing dehazed images with improved visibility, contrast, and sharpness. The proposed method demonstrates significant potential for applications in underwater exploration, marine biology, and robotic vision.

articleTitle: Development of a Cost-Effective and Portable Digital Storage Oscilloscope Using Raspberry Pi Pico and Mobile App
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a cost-effective and portable Digital Storage Oscilloscope (DSO) utilizing the Raspberry Pi Pico microcontroller in conjunction with the Scoppy Android application. The proposed system establishes a robust communication interface via USB OTG, facilitating efficient data transfer and real-time signal analysis. By integrating the Raspberry Pi Pico with the Scoppy platform, the system delivers a viable alternative to conventional DSOs, offering real-time waveform visualization and advanced measurement capabilities. The Scoppy application's user-friendly interface supports precise adjustments, including time-per-division and voltage scaling, ensuring an intuitive user experience. This work aims to lower the accessibility barrier to high-performance measurement tools, thereby fostering innovation and advancing experimentation in electronics design and development.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Interference Constrained NOMA in 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to analyze the achievable rate in the power domain non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) technique for communication between six devices through an Internet-of-Things (IoT) gateway device. In this study, we first derive the expressions for the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) and Signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) for the transmission between the devices, which are crucial to determine the overall system performance. The analysis also takes into account the impact of co-channel interference (CCI) at the relay node, a significant factor that affects communication reliability in NOMA systems. Furthermore, we investigate how various system parameters such as distance, transmit power, and path loss exponent influence the achievable rate, considering the dynamic nature of wireless environments. By optimizing power allocation and addressing the challenges of interference, the system can achieve higher throughput and improved reliability. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the performance of NOMA in the context of IoT system framework, offering insights into the trade-offs involved in achieving high data rates while ensuring energy efficiency. The results are discussed in terms of the systems' response to changes in key parameters, with the goal of optimizing performance for practical IoT deployments.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Induced Selective Identification of Dopamine Using Doped Carbon Quantum Dots
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The present work highlights the selective identification of dopamine (DA) with machine learning (ML) classification. Dopamine is an essential organic neurotransmitter that acts a dynamic role. With the inhouse experimental da-ta, the ML models are trained with more than thirty classification algorithms for the efficient selection of DA among various metal ions and biomolecules that exist in human body fluids. The experimental data was collected by measuring the turn-off photoluminescence intensity of nitrogen-doped car-bon quantum dots in the presence of various metal ions and biomolecules. A promising agreement between predicted result and experimental consequences endorses the effectiveness of the proposed ML prediction. Additionally, confusion matrices and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) are introduced to validate the outcomes by visual analysis.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Driven Framework for Flood Risk Index Calculation
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The Earth is hit by several catastrophic events every day bringing with itself devastation which amounts to crores. This paper is aimed at expediting the calculation of FRI by breaking it into two supportive components FHI & FVI which are determined separately using machine learning algorithms. For FHI, factors like total rainfall, event frequency, catchment area and soil absorption rating are used which are finally fed into a statistical machine-learning model for prediction. For FVI, factors used include maximum rainfall in 24 hours, population density, total agricultural land and total hardscape area. The latter two are extracted directly from the satellite image of the area.

articleTitle: Optimizing Drug Management: AI-Driven Pharmacy Analytics and Electronic Health Records
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The integration of pharmacy analytic with Electronic Health Record (EHR) is a revolutionary development in the domain of medical field. This paper explores the benefits, methodologies, challenges and highlighting the role of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) in optimizing this integration. Additionally, it also consists of a brief study and comparisons on various types of Machine learning models along with their accuracy to forecast the outcomes that are needed to enhance drug management by combining EHR data with pharmacy operations. To protect patient safety, privacy, and trust, the ethical ramifications of combining pharmacy and EHR data are investigated.

articleTitle: Review on Substrate Integrated Suspended Line Based Filters with Stub Loaded Hexagonal Shaped Low Pass Filter
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: A multilayered realization of circuits using embedded cavities is done in substrate integrated suspended line (SISL) technology. With the emerging developments in the RF and Microwave communication systems, the role of filters is very important. As most of the frequency bands are currently in use for various applications, it is important to select the exact frequency of design and cut off the undesired band from the circuit. This paper presents a review on the SISL based filters and their performance comparison. A compact elliptical LPF is proposed based on SISL whose performance is enhanced by including open shunt stubs. Introduction of three stubs symmetrically on either side of the filter resulted in extra three transmission zeros in the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> response. The filter realizes a pass band from 0-2.6 GHz with the perfect rejection and roll off of 180dB/GHz.

articleTitle: Few-Shot Learning for Early Detection of Laryngeal Cancer with Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Early diagnosis of laryngeal cancer significantly relates to prognosis and treatment. This work presents a classification model that uses very few-shot learning where classification between healthy and early-stage cancerous tissues can be done accurately even with very limited data. The proposed approach relies on an expert-curated dataset of 1,320 image patches of size 100x100 pixels, which suggests promising potential for real-world applications, especially in strictly limited amounts of annotated medical images. This approach uses Explainable AI (XAI) to increase the transparency of the model and eventually enhance clinical trust in the predictions obtained with that model. This technique has the promise for early detection, but it also has high accuracy and further allows clinical thinking into the decision mechanism of the model. That is a future direction for developing the refined version of such a technique to develop robustness and application in different clinical settings.

articleTitle: A Basic Framework for Fetal Monitoring in Detecting Stillbirth Risks Using Heart Rate and Fetal Movements
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Stillbirth remains a critical issue in obstetrics, with various underlying factors contributing to fetal mortality. Early detection of potential risks can significantly improve clinical outcomes. This paper presents a simple framework for detecting stillbirth risks using fetal heart rate and fetal movement data. The framework is implemented as a Java-based software system that analyzes heart rate and fetal movement data, offering a preliminary model for monitoring fetal health. This approach aims to support clinicians in their decision-making process and foster further development of more sophisticated monitoring systems in the future. The proposed system is not intended to replace medical professionals but rather serves as an auxiliary tool for early detection of potential stillbirth risks based on available monitoring data.

articleTitle: Solar PV-Based Power Conversion System: A Real-Time Testing Facility
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This article proposes a real-time testing facility for solar PV-based power conversion systems developed at Laval University, Quebec, Canada. A detailed description of key objectives of the laboratory and microgrid test setup along with testing facilities such as simulation and experimental, has been provided in this article. The developed microgrid test setup consists of the utility grid, Opal-RT based power-hardware-in-loop (PHIL), solar PV emulator-based solar generator and a regenerative electronic load. This article explains different modes of operation and configuration for testing different components and control solar PV power conversion systems. Finally, simulation results based on MATLAB/Simulink under different operating conditions have been described to demonstrate the performance of the developed test setup.

articleTitle: Advanced Attendance Monitoring: A Unified System Using QR Codes and Facial Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This paper presents a very new approach toward attendance tracking in any educational institution that integrates QR code technology with facial recognition. The proposed solution tries to make attendance recording more accurate and efficient, avoiding inaccuracies and administrative difficulties from prior techniques. In this approach, students first register themselves at the institution; subsequently, their information and photograph are taken. After that, a special QR code is generated, getting printed on their institutional ID card, which would serve as a unique identification. Students scan QR codes while entering and exiting premises, followed by face recognition in verification. The technology calculates percentages of attendance based on entry and exit timestamps. The information collected thereafter gets stored in a structured student database, which tracks a student's progress according to their academic cycle. This paper reviews the technique, applications of facial recognition technology, and the benefits the system provides as a whole. This research looks into the future and studies prospective applications and updates to this technology.

articleTitle: Machining Parameter of Jute/Kenaf/Glass Fibre With SiO2 Hybrid Polymer Composite using RSM
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: In the increasingly competitive manufacturing market, businesses try to develop high-quality products with lowest expenditures and in less time. Because of their numerous components, each with distinct properties, composite materials are increasingly gaining popularity. Key considerations when focusing on these composite materials are environmental kindness, lightweight nature, and amazing particular qualities. Natural resource fibers are blended with synthetic fibers to generate hybrid composites that are eco-friendly to some extent to fulfill these needs. Glass, Kenaf, and jute Fibres are utilized as reinforcing in an epoxy resin matrix in these composites. Dealing with such composite materials, however, presents complications, particularly in drilling procedures as compared to metals. This is because of the alternate layers of array and reinforcement, which have unique properties. To address these issues, an automated feed drilling machine is used to conduct an experiment, which has a multi-component piezo-electric dynamometer. A coated carbide drill is utilized for the drilling operation. The main objective of this research is to demonstrate how variations in tool diameter, feed rate, and spindle speed affect the machining characteristics of these hybrid composites through Response surface methodology. A profile projector is used to analyze the effects of drilling, such as material degradation. The data show that all of the previously listed parameters have a part throughout the drilling procedure and that altering the feed rate is useful in reducing the caused damage and confirmed by optimization through Response surface methodology.

articleTitle: Verifying the Robustness of Fingerprint Authentication Method for FSO System Against Atmospheric Turbulence and Obstructions
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: For Free Space Optical Communication system, in order to check the origin of the received data stream an authentication method has been proposed, which uses the number of intertwined phase fronts of a vortex beam as its ‘Fingerprint’. The stability of this method has been checked for transmission of the beam through highly turbulent atmosphere, as well as partial obstruction. For atmospheric turbulence simulation, Karman-Tatarski model was used. The robustness of the process was tested for additional obstructions whose percentage was increased gradually in order to find the limiting amount of obstruction.

articleTitle: Comparative Study on Different Types of Solar Based Water Pumping Systems for Driving 1hp Single Phase Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Water pumping systems are used for irrigation, livestock watering and village water supplying. Pumping water is the life line of farmers. It plays an important role in modern agriculture which ensures the sufficient distribution of water across the lands under cultivation in a very efficient way. For this purpose electric energy or fossil fuel like diesel is used generally to run the water pumping system. But in remote areas farmers are facing frequent power cut, moreover, in some areas there is no supply of electricity. In case of fossil fuel driven system objectionable gases are emitted which cause environmental pollution. Therefore, the trend of using solar energy is getting popular in recent days. In this paper three different types of solar based water pumping systems have been discussed with comparative analysis. Each system is designed to power a single phase induction motor with 1horsepower (hp) capacity which drives the pumping system. These solar power generating systems are on-grid, off-grid and VFD solar systems. The study shows their design, construction and installation techniques in detail. A comparative cost analysis of primary investment of these solar based water pumping systems has also been mentioned in this paper.

articleTitle: Event Identification and Chronology Model of Ramayana
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The paper introduces an event chronology model for Hindu mythological texts, with a focus on the Ramayana's Bala-kanda. It captures and structures sentence-level events based on their chronological order to better understand narrative progression and character interactions. A manually crafted dataset of 1217 events, involving 214 characters across 75 chapters, is used to generate a knowledge graph. The graph organizes events by sequence, linking characters, actions, and chapters within the storyline. The event chronology is mapped by establishing relationships between events, ensuring they are connected in the proper sequence to reflect the narrative flow. This approach enables a deeper understanding of how each event contributes to the overarching story, providing insights into both the individual actions of characters and their significance within the broader mythological narrative. Transformer-based models (BERT, DistilBERT, and RoBERTa) were utilized for predicting subsequent events, with RoBERTa showing the highest accuracy in preserving the correct event chronology. This structure is key to analyzing the sequential development of the Ramayana's storyline.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of Gravity Battery: A Breakthrough in Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The growing demand for sustainable and renewable energy solutions has sparked interest in energy storage systems that prioritize efficiency and environmental sustainability. Among these innovations, gravity-based energy storage systems, commonly referred to as gravity batteries, emerge as a promising technology. This paper details the design and construction of a prototype gravity battery that harnesses potential energy by lifting a mass, which can subsequently be released to generate electricity on demand. The research delves into the fundamental principles of gravity energy storage, encompassing gravitational potential energy, the conversion of mechanical energy to electrical energy, and strategies for optimizing efficiency. The design phase involves the careful selection of materials for the mass, pulley system, and generator, taking into account factors such as energy density, durability, and costeffectiveness. Challenges encountered during fabrication, including frictional losses, stability, and load-bearing capacity, are addressed through a process of iterative testing and refinement. The prototype is evaluated for its efficiency, scalability, and practical use in off-grid and backup power applications. Results suggest that gravity batteries hold considerable promise for small to medium-scale energy storage solutions and could provide a sustainable alternative to conventional chemical batteries, particularly in areas where geographical or structural conditions favor the utilization of gravitational energy. This research advances the field of energy storage by showcasing a practical, lowmaintenance approach that utilizes fundamental mechanical principles, with potential benefits for energy access in rural areas and the development of sustainable urban infrastructure. Future research avenues include scaling the system, enhancing efficiency through advanced materials and mechanics, and exploring the integration of gravity batteries with renewable energy systems.

articleTitle: Investigation on PCA and LDA Feature Extraction Algorithms with KNN Classifier Targetting to Improve Diagnostic Accuracy into Detection of Breast Cancer Malignancy
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This work aims to compare two different Feature Extraction Algorithms (FEAs) viz. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), using a K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) classifier on the breast cancer Wisconsin (diagnostic) dataset, taken from the UC Irvine machine learning repository. The dataset was divided into a training and test dataset, by selecting 50, 60, 70 and 80% of the whole samples present into the dataset, respectively as the training dataset. The execution was deployed in ‘Google Colab Notebook’ and ‘Anaconda Navigator’, supporting Python 3.6 programming language. For both models, the most accurate values were found for 80% of the training dataset level. PCA provided the best accuracy as 97.37%. A total of 9 quality performance metric parameters such as sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative likelihood ratios, positive and negative predictive values, diagnostic odds ratio, Youden's index and F-1 score, were also obtained for the 80% training dataset level.

articleTitle: Perfomance Improvement of mpdCNN as Ensemble Learning Model on Low Resolution Image-Face Recognition System
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Low resolution image-face recognition system is one of the challenging aspects of face recognition models' development. From machine learning, deep learning, and into ensemble learning are implemented to develop face recognition models. Including mpdCNN that published by Mishra in a journal article. This mpdCNN already achieved 88.6% accuracy score on SCFace dataset while published. Based on literature review, ensemble learning model can be improved by modifying parallel layers. The purpose of this research is to improve mpdCNN's performance by implementing some modifications include adding parallel layers, alternating the fusion layers, expanding the layers, and adding residual connections. Some modifications were successfully improved mpdCNN's accuracy score. By adding parallel layers and residual connections into mpdCNN's architecture, the modified mpdCNN that proposed in this research achieved 92.33% accuracy score, measured by Rank-k evaluation metric.

articleTitle: Modeling and Characterization of $Al_{0.8}ln_{0.15}Ga_{0.05}N/\text{GaN}$ HEMTs With Enhanced 2DEG Density for High-Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: In this research work, we focused on improving the 2-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) concentration in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Al_{0.8}In_{0.15}Ga_{0.05}N/\text{GaN}$</tex> HEMTs to improve device performance. The HEMT design incorporates <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Al_{0.8}In_{0.15}Ga_{0.05}N$</tex> as the barrier material, deviating from the conventional GaN HEMT. This modification results in a notable 9.6% increase in the 2DEG concentration within the device structure. The heightened 2DEG concentration is attributed to the inherent spontaneous and piezoelectric polarization effects occurring at the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Al_{0.8}In_{0.15}Ga_{0.05}N/\text{GaN}$</tex> interface. With improved transfer characteristics and output behavior, the novel HEMT design presents a compelling avenue for further exploration in high-power applications.

articleTitle: Predictive Modelling for Chronic Kidney Disease: A Hybrid Approach Using Exploratory Data Analysis, Machine Learning and Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is a growing health crisis in India, affecting nearly 17% of the population. Due to its often asymptomatic nature, CKD is frequently diagnosed only in advanced stages, leading to expensive treatments and poor patient outcomes. To address this, we explore the potential of AI and machine learning to enhance early detection and predict CKD progression, enabling timely interventions. This paper presents a Machine Learning (ML) model with Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) for CKD prediction, emphasizing both accuracy and interpretability, which is critical for clinical adoption. We integrate Explainable AI (XAI) techniques, specifically LIME, to provide healthcare professionals with clear insights into model predictions, promoting trust and transparency. Our approach combines predictive power with interpretability, offering a practical solution for early CKD detection and improving clinical decision-making. We discuss the challenges and future directions of integrating AI in healthcare, with the aim of reducing CKD-related healthcare costs and improving patient outcomes in India.

articleTitle: Design of a Flexible Metasurface based dual Bandpass Filter in ISM and 5G cellular band for Bio-medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This paper provides a detailed and concise view of a single layered, flexible metasurface (MS)-based slot type dual bandpass filter for ISM and cellular 5G bands. The unit cell of the MS structure comprises three different slots designed on a flexible jeans substrate. The proposed structure provides two distinct transmission bands at 2.4 GHz and 4.5 GHz respectively. Additionally, one stop-band has also been realized at 3.2 GHz; thereby making the structure suitable for wearable antenna applications. Analysis of the structure under varying incident angles is done to find the stable performance of the structure up to 45⁰. The electric field distributions have been studied to understand the functions of the different slots in the MS design. Such low-profile, along with the compact design makes the structure suitable for being a wearable spatial filter. All the simulations of the work, along with the results have been performed and analysed using ANSYS HFSS v2024.

articleTitle: One Cycle Controlled 3-Phase Inverter
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This paper presents a One Cycle Control technique for a 3-phase inverter. One Cycle Control (OCC) is a nonlinear control technique that controls the ON time of a switch within one switching cycle. The OCC technique is applied here for a 3-phase full bridge inverter. Each leg has been controlled individually with a 120° phase-shifted sinusoidal reference wave. Theoretically, the OCC technique has an inherent property of Dead time distortion compensation without using any current sensor. A modified integrator circuit is applied to this 3-phase inverter circuit, which reduces the resetting error and improves the Total Harmonic distortion of output voltage (THD). In case of fluctuations in DC bus the OCC technique has the feature of correcting the error in the output due to this fluctuation within one switching cycle. It is easily implementable using discrete hardware which is very easy and cost-effective. The proposed technique validated via digital simulation hardware implementation.

articleTitle: Recurrent Neural Network Model to Predict and Monitor Student Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Academic metrics are very important for monitoring and tracking student achievement, helping to improve instructional quality and expand learning outcomes. There are difficulties in producing indicators and enhancing the precision of student performance prediction models using the assessment data that is currently available. Nonetheless, it assists teachers in adapting their instructional strategies and interventions to the particular needs of each student. As a result, addressing these challenges is crucial for better efficacy and improving students' academic success. We intend to create five recommended machine learning models as case studies to predict academic success for student performance monitoring and tracking. The model seeks to capture the complicated visualizations and dependencies inherent in the sequential structure of grades throughout a course. This research investigates the development of a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) model to predict student performance using a data set of results from several examinations. We explore generic machine learning approaches, followed by an in depth look at RNNs, their application to our job, and code implementation. Finally, we evaluate the performance of our model, draw conclusions, and discuss further improvements. Our findings are unique and encouraging. This update improves clarity and flow while still conveying the idea of performance monitoring.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Corrugated Vivaldi Antenna for Enhanced 5G Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a corrugated Vivaldi antenna optimized for enhanced 5G wireless communication. The antenna operates within a wide frequency range of 2–13 GHz, achieving a significant return loss of -33.323 dB at 6.9519 GHz. By introducing corrugations along the radiating edges and a circular stub at the top, the design optimizes impedance matching, bandwidth, and directivity. Simulation results confirm the antenna's suitability for high-speed, reliable 5G connectivity, highlighting its potential application in next-generation communication systems.

articleTitle: Generating Images from Text Using GANs vs Transformers
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This paper compares Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and transformer-based models for text-to-image generation, examining each approach's ability to convert textual descriptions into realistic images. GANs, leveraging a generator-discriminator framework, have made strides with models like DF-GAN [1] and StackGAN [2], which improve image fidelity through multi-stage generation and attention. However, GANs face challenges with complex datasets. Transformer-based models, initially used in natural language processing, offer robust handling of dependencies, enhancing the capture of image features from text. Emerging hybrid models combine GAN and transformer strengths for improved stability and image quality. This study aims to identify optimal techniques by analyzing their architectures, training, and output quality, contributing to advancements in multi-modal generative modeling.

articleTitle: Real-Time Virtual Classroom Platform: Integrating React, Firebase, WebRTC, and Socket.io
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This paper discusses the process of creating a virtual classroom platform. The main goal of this platform is to provide students and teachers uninterrupted learning experiences. React JS is used for designing the frontend part, and Firebase is used for authentication and storing data like classroom details and study materials, etc. WebRTC and Socket.io are used in real-time video conferencing and messaging systems. This platform helps teachers to share assignments, announcements, and course materials. This platform is built to accomplish the requirement for the environments of online learning, which makes learning more adaptable, engaging, and effective. WebRTC and Socket.io offer high-quality, real-time group video calling features, and Firebase is used for data storage for course materials and assignments. Socket.io also provides a reliable real-time messaging system at the time of video conferencing, which helps to have an interactive learning experience for the students and teachers. This paper discusses the main concepts, technical architecture, challenges faced during the implementation process, testing, and its outcomes, and the future scopes of this platform, which include the capability of handling a large number of users in video conferences and adding analytics features.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Capacitance Model of Silicon-Based Commercial Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The continuous improvement in solar cell efficiency necessitates a comprehensive analysis of their dynamic performance under varying environmental conditions. The stochastic nature of real-time illumination intensity significantly impacts the dynamic behavior of the latest commercially available solar cells, particularly those utilizing PERC (Passivated Emitter and Rear Cell) technology with improved open-circuit voltage. Real-time performance of these advanced solar cells is influenced by both structural design and material parameters along with the environmental parameters. While the impact of temperature variation on open-circuit voltage is well established, capturing the effects of fluctuating illumination conditions is crucial for accurately evaluating performance in driving subsequent circuitry. This paper presents an analytically derived compact model that provides a detailed understanding of the dynamic operation of silicon-based commercial solar cells. It specifically estimates the dynamic capacitance under varying illumination intensities while maintaining a fixed temperature. The model offers critical insights into the dynamic performance of PERC technology solar cells, thereby enabling more effective optimization and deployment in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Dynamic Multilingual Voice Transcription Using NLP
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This research paper presents a method for preparing natural language data for analysis, with a particular focus on converting spoken language into written form within a Language Variation framework. The proposed method seeks to maintain the accuracy of the primary linguistic data being studied, while offering a theoretically sound and practical approach to data preparation. The method is designed to be efficient, placing reasonable constraints on the time and resources required from the analyst. Additionally, this project aims to provide clear, actionable guidelines for transcribing linguistic data from speech to text, fostering data-sharing within the linguistic community and facilitating broader research collaborations.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Compact Millimeter-Wave Vivaldi Antenna for Wearable WBAN Application
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: A novel low-profile antenna, designed for operation in the millimeter-wave frequencies in WBANs at 32.5 GHz, is presented. Optimized to be compact in a form factor of approximately 7 × 10 mm with height 0.79mm for body-worn devices, which is a crucial area with vast space constraints, it has an efficiency for short-distance optical interactions in wearables that do not allow rough wireless performances. This is the small size of the antenna that allows it to support high-speed and low-latency communication; hence, it can be used for real-time data transfer in WBANs. This design contributes to wearable technology advancement by achieving a balance between performance, energy efficiency, and compactness for a wide range of applications, including health, fitness, and smart wearable devices.

articleTitle: Delay-Optimized High-Speed Dynamic Comparator with Temperature Compensation
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Dynamic comparators are essential for enabling the fast and accurate performance needed by analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) in today's communication systems. However, conventional designs often suffer from performance degradation at low input difference voltages and significant delay variations under temperature fluctuations, which many designers tend to ignore. This paper proposes an improved dynamic comparator design that addresses these challenges by integrating a cascode cross-coupled configuration within the pre-amplifier section to enhance gain and ensure reliable operation at small input differences. Additionally, a temperature compensation circuit is introduced at the latch stage to mitigate the impact of temperature variations on delay. In the proposed dynamic comparator, the i) propagation delay is decreased by 35.51% and 58.21%, and the ii) delay variation at different temperatures is decreased by 36.17% and 68.22% in comparison with the re-implemented cascode cross-coupled dynamic comparator and conventional dynamic comparator, respectively.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis of (10,0) Coaxial Carbon Nanotube Field Effect Transistor based on Electronic Properties and Device Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The electronic properties of Carbon Nanotube Field-Effect Transistors (CNTFETs) vary based on the chirality and chirality vector values. This study investigates the electronic properties and performance of CNTFETs using zigzag (10,0) chirality as the channel material in coaxial configuration. The analysis encompasses key electronic properties such as I-V characteristics, energy states, transmission efficiency, position and density of the CNTFET. Critical parameters including the cut-off voltage, output conductance, channel length modulation, ON-OFF current ratio, threshold voltage, and sub-threshold slope are calculated to evaluate device performance. The CNTFET demonstrates excellent performance, highlighted a low threshold voltage of 0.3 V, and a subthreshold slope of 60.4 mV/decade. These findings of (10,0) CNTFET imply significant potential for low-power applications.

articleTitle: Prompt Driven Image Creation: A Comparative Evaluation of Generative AI Tools
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of four generative AI models namely ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, and Stable Diffusion - evaluated on metrics such as visual quality, prompt adherence, creativity, usability, and processing time. Visual and quantitative results highlight Gemini and Copilot's superiority in artistic and imaginative tasks, while Stable Diffusion excels in customization for advanced users. ChatGPT demonstrates ease of use but is limited in complexity. We also provides the best practices in selecting and using such tools to improve creative work. This study emphasizes the importance of evaluating generative AI tools based on diverse requirements and practical use cases.

articleTitle: Study of Mangrove Forests Using Google Earth Engine
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Mangrove forests are crucial ecosystems that provide valuable goods and services while serving as carbon sinks. These ecosystems act as natural buffers against coastal erosion, mitigate the impacts of climate change, and support diverse biodiversity. However, they are increasingly threatened by rising sea levels, changing salinity patterns, and anthropogenic activities such as deforestation and urbanization. Monitoring the health of mangrove forests is critical for ensuring their conservation and long-term sustainability. This study investigates vegetation dynamics in a selected region using satellite-derived indices, specifically the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and the Normalized Difference Chlorophyll Index (NDCI).

articleTitle: Fine-Tuning Vision Transformer Using LoRA for Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This research paper focuses on fine-tuning a Vision Transformer (ViT) model using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) for image classification tasks. LoRA offers an efficient alternative to traditional fine-tuning by significantly reducing the number of trainable parameters and training time while maintaining competitive accuracy. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has revolutionized numerous domains by enabling machines to perform tasks that typically require human intelligence, such as perception and decision-making. Large Language Models (LLMs), like GPT, have demonstrated the power of transformers in NLP, while Vision Transformers (ViTs) extend this paradigm to computer vision by utilizing self-attention mechanisms for global feature extraction. The study employs two distinct datasets: Food101, a large-scale dataset with 101,000 images across various food categories, and Cats vs. Dogs, a binary classification dataset. By leveraging LoRA, we demonstrate the feasibility of adapting a pretrained ViT model to specialized image recognition tasks with minimal computational overhead. The results highlight a remarkable reduction in model size, a significant decrease in the number of trainable parameters, and competitive accuracy, underscoring LoRA's potential for efficient deployment on devices with limited resources. These findings pave the way for future personalized AI applications in resource-constrained environments.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a PV System with Battery Storage Using Bifacial Halfcut Module
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: In the absence of conventional energy sources renewable energy is the only suitable option left. Multiple renewable energy sources like Hydroelectric Energy, Tidal Energy, Geothermal Energy, and Solar Electrical Energy are becoming popular every day. There are multiple reasons such as its availability in small to large sizes, predictability, easy installation, smooth maintenance process, drop in system installation cost, and mostly fast return on investment. With the increase in demand for solar photovoltaic panels, the demand for producing higher power output from less area is increasing rapidly. Hence with every breakthrough, the efficiency of the Photovoltaic Panel is increasing rapidly. With continuous development, the PV modules are developed in such a way that light can be absorbed from the front and rear on both sides. In the Bi-facial module, the direct sunlight gets absorbed from the front, and the albedo is also absorbed from the back to increase the power generation further. With the implementation of half-cut technology, the shading losses are minimized further. Rapid development is also being done on MPPT and Inverter to improve efficiency. Presently a generalized mathematical model for bifacial half-cut module is not published in any literature. In this paper, the research gap is covered by designing a Bifacial Half-cut PV Module along with an MPPT and also a bidirectional DC-DC Converter for charging and discharging of Battery Bank. Finally, we have integrated the system and also have simulated the designed system to check its stability. Such a model helps in analyzing and validating performance characteristics of commercially available bifacial modules and half-cut modules.

articleTitle: Lithium-Ion Batteries in EVs: Comparative Analysis and BMS Innovations
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EV) are proving to be an efficient technology in the world with their propulsion being powered fully or mostly by electricity which is a viable alternative to fossil fuel-based cars (in an environment-friendly way). These cars are responsible for the reduction of air pollution and reduction of global warming due to the greenhouse gases emitted by fossil fuel-based cars. Thus, maintaining a sustainable and efficient power source for them is crucial.

articleTitle: AUTHENTISCAN: Prototype Design of Novel, Compact, Cost-Effective, Portable, Sustainable IOT-Enabled Biometric Attendance Tool
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This research aims to design a novel IOT-enabled, portable attendance tool kit hardware prototype using Fingerprint-based Biometric technologies instead of conventional RFID based technologies. This research contributes in the development of efficient and secure attendance management system suitable for educational institutions, businesses, and other organizations. The main objective for such implementation is to incorporate all the features like portability, lightweight, and reliability within the IOT-enabled compact attendance tool kit comprised of nodeMCU ESP8266, R307 fingerprint module and LCD display. This portable module is connected to the server using wireless connections for transferring the input fingerprint data. This secure device is capable of providing better accuracy and efficiency in tracking and managing attendance records. The system employs a centralized database for storing a maximum of 1000 entries as well as processing attendance data to provide real-time monitoring and generate comprehensive reports for administrators. The attendance details are obtained from the device and are showcased on the website of the organization. The novelty of the IOT enabled proposed device lies in enhanced features like portability and cost effective in comparison with other attendance tool kit available in the market.

articleTitle: Design and Cost Analysis of Solar UPS Based 3kWp Off-Grid Solar System with Generation of 12–15 Units/day for 2.5kW Household Load
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Solar energy is one of the most important renewable energy resources. Advancement of solar technology leads to use solar power as much as possible to prevent the depletion of natural resources like coal, fossil fuels, etc. and reduce the cost of electric energy consumed for different purposes. Use of solar technology keeps environment clean. Generally electric power is needed to run household load and for this consumer should pay monthly electricity bill to the Electricity Distribution Companies. To reduce the home electricity consumption which in turn reduces the charge of monthly electricity bill of a consumer on-grid solar and off-grid solar technologies are available which can be installed. In this paper, design of a 3kWp off-grid solar system with all its component details and installation technique has been discussed. The sole purpose is to generate solar power that is fed to the load coming from the utilization of home appliances. The designed system is capable to generate 12–15 units of energy per day with 10 hours battery backup-time. In this system we have considered MPPT solar UPS (inverter) for improving the efficiency of the entire system. For better performance, Mono PERC half cut solar panels are highly recommended for this proposed system. The main objective of this paper is to show how off-grid solar system can reduce the charge of monthly electricity bill. A detail cost analysis has also been discussed in this paper. Initial investment for installation of off-grid solar system is very high. But in the long run consumer can profit from it.

Author Keywords: Mono PERC half cut PV panel

articleTitle: A Microstrip Antenna with Shifting of Bandwidth Using Slitting a Portion and Slotting of Radiating Patch
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: In this research work, a low-profile microstrip patch antenna has been designed with a circular radiating patch. A portion of the radiating patch has been slitted to shift the resonating band towards a higher frequency range. A slot has been introduced on the radiating patch to shift the resonating band towards a lower frequency range. The distinctive feature of this antenna design is the shifting of the resonant band towards a higher frequency range or lower frequency range as per requirement using slitting a portion or slotting of the circular radiating patch. Before slitting of the radiating patch, the resonant band of the antenna was (3.4-3.69GHz) for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(S_{11}\leq-10$</tex> dB) usable for WiMAX (3.4-3.69GHz) application band, and after slitting, the resonant band shifted to (4.19-4.49GHz) usable for (4.2-4.4 GHz) Aeronautical radio navigation service (ARNS) application band. After the introduction of slot on the radiating patch the resonant band shifted to (3.2-3.42GHz) usable for LTE(3.2-3.3 GHz) and WiMAX (3.3-3.4GHz) application band. The design and modification of the antenna has been done using theoretical calculation and HFSS simulation software. After that, it has been fabricated and different parameters have been measured using Vector Network Analyser. It has been found that the measured results are very much similar to the simulated results.

articleTitle: Advancements in Weather Monitoring System: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This review provides an in-depth analysis of recent advancements and key trends in weather monitoring systems. It emphasizes the progress made in technologies and highlights their significant contributions to the field. These systems are essential tools for collecting and interpreting atmospheric data to predict and monitor weather conditions, supporting applications such as disaster management, agriculture, aviation, and climate research. The review investigates modern sensor innovations, IoT-enabled systems, and remote sensing technologies that have transformed real-time data collection and analysis. It discusses advancements in performance factors, including accuracy, scalability, energy efficiency, and costeffectiveness. Furthermore, the paper explores advanced topics like machine learning-driven weather prediction, satellite-based observation systems, and the integration of cloud computing for improved data processing capabilities. Challenges such as hardware constraints, data reliability, and integration complexities are also examined, along with potential strategies to overcome them. By synthesizing existing research, this study offers valuable insights for professionals in the field, helping them enhance and innovate weather monitoring systems. The findings provide overview of present state-of-the-art technologies and propose directions for future research and development, emphasizing the importance of this field in addressing global challenges.

articleTitle: Quantum Dot-Based Real-Time Disease Detection Using Embedded Systems: A Novel Approach for Portable Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to real-time disease diagnostics using a microcontroller integrated quantum dot sensor device. Quantum dots, renowned for their high sensitivity and precise fluorescence properties, are deployed to detect specific biomarkers in biological samples, offering rapid and accurate health diagnostics. This work lays the foundation for future advancements in embedded systems for biomedical applications, offering an efficient and low-cost solution to improve patient outcomes through timely intervention.

articleTitle: User Preference Based Cumulative Trust (UPBCT) Computation Model
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Cloud Computing is the biggest buzz word in the Computer and Information Technology industries. Almost every IT organization has adopted cloud computing technologies. There are multiple Cloud Service Providers (CSP) in the market like Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), IBM Cloud (Kyndryl) and many more. Every CSP provides various cloud services to Cloud Users (CU). It is a big challenge today for cloud users to decide on which CSP will be suitable for their requirements. Trust values for cloud services helps cloud users to choose the most suitable cloud service and CSP. Trust computation has several methodologies like reputation based, SLA verification based, selfassessment based, policy based, societal trust based, and evidence based. Among all these methodologies, evidence-based trust computation is considered as the effective and most trustworthy as it computes the trust values based on QoS attributes of the cloud services. We have studied many of evidence-based models proposed by various researchers. Among many we found that the approach of weightage-based normalization of QoS attribute values is more effective and accurate while calculating the trust values. Also, we found that these models are missing on what user is expecting with respect to values of QoS attributes. Accordingly, in this paper we have proposed a UPBCT computation model which is evidence-based, follows weightage-based normalization of QoS attribute values approach, and takes in account the user preferred values for QoS attributes. The results support the efficiency of the proposed model compared to other models, helps cloud users to choose better cloud service as per their requirements and helps CSP with the desired value for QoS attributes so that they can enhance their cloud services to meet those desired values of QoS attributes and increase the trust values of their cloud services.

articleTitle: Low Power Multiplier Using NAND Logic Cells
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Different models of multiplier that offer the least power consumption are designed as technology node changes. The motive of the designers is to work on the minimization of power with less penalty in speed and area. The main focus of the present development is on the low power multiplier design for the different applications. This paper proposes a method of an efficient Wallace Tree Multiplier which is power efficient and uses a 7:3 counter consisting of full adders implemented using the NAND Logic cells. This proposed design is synthesized in the Cadence Genus tool which uses a 45 nm technology library cell in CMOS. The detailed comparison is performed between two multipliers in which one is designed using 2: 1 multiplexers and Exor gates that already exist and the other using NAND Logic cells which is proposed for 4-bit operands. The proposed design of the multiplier which uses NAND logic cells shows that it takes less power and has less delay when it is compared to the multiplier which uses 2: 1 Multiplexers and Exor gates. This design gives a good performance for both FPGA and ASIC platforms.

articleTitle: IoT-Enhanced Battery Management System: Real-Time Monitoring, Predictive Analytics and Safety Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Using Internet of Things (IoT) the use of battery management system (BMS) has been redefined for real time engagement. The BMS is multi-functional and works effectively across a range of industries, integrating sensors, microcontrollers, modules and cloud servers enabling the technology to track parameters including location and state of charge with strong precision and protecting against mishaps through early warnings. This greatly aids in the reduction of maintenance costs while also increasing the battery longevity while managing the charging and discharging cycles with high efficiency. Moreover, machine learning algorithms have also been embedded in the system, allowing it to learn over time and enhance its forecast performance overtime for metrics such as Remaining Useful Life and capacity retention predictive analytics, greatly improving safety and performance levels. This paper goes into a deep exploration of how the system works, its design and architecture while also evaluating the proposed systems battery efficiency, reliability and environmental impact.

articleTitle: AURA: Advancing Human-Robot Interaction Through Unified Voice and Gesture Control
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI) assistants has revolutionized human-machine interaction, but traditional systems often rely on singular input modalities such as voice commands. This project, AURA: AI Robot with Unified Voice and Gesture Control, integrates voice and air gesture recognition to create a seamless and intuitive user interface. Utilizing a Raspberry Pi, camera, speaker, and microphone, the system combines computer vision and natural language processing to interpret user commands dynamically. The AI assistant is designed to respond accurately to both vocal instructions and gestures, enabling hands-free and voice-free operation in various scenarios. AURA's innovative approach enhances accessibility, convenience, and user experience, with potential applications in smart homes, healthcare, and personal robotics. This unified control mechanism demonstrates the future of multimodal interaction, emphasizing efficiency and adaptability in AI-driven systems.

articleTitle: SIW Antenna with Cavity Backed Feature and Integrated Connected U Slot for Satellite Application Band
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The research concept explores the frequency band characteristics of a cavity-backed SIW, or substrate integrated waveguide antenna, and goes into detail about its development. A connected U slot is included for the satellite application frequency band. It has a gain of 3.12 dBi and resonance frequency of 10.71 GHz within satellite application band range.

articleTitle: Advancements in Deep Learning for Smart Surveillance: A Survey on Crime and Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The increasing prevalence of advanced surveillance technologies has spurred significant research in automated anomaly detection systems using deep learning. This survey synthesizes recent developments across various distinct studies addressing diverse security challenges. These include theft detection using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with object tracking, robbery identification using convolutional LSTM models trained on the UNI-Crime dataset, anomaly detection leveraging weakly supervised learning on UCF-Crime data, and weapon recognition using YOLOv3. Several other approaches demonstrate significant accuracy and efficiency improvements, achieving accuracies. Despite varying datasets and architectures, the integration of CNNs, YOLO, and LSTM models reflects a shared emphasis on spatial-temporal feature extraction for real-time applications. This paper provides a comparative analysis of these methodologies, highlighting the role of dataset quality, transfer learning, and computational efficiency in advancing smart surveillance systems to mitigate crime and enhance public safety.

articleTitle: Fetal Health Classification Using Machine Learning on Cardiotocography Data
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This study explores a machine learning approach for detecting and classifying fetal health which is a crucial aspect in ensuring proper care and wellbeing of both fetus and the mother. The conventional diagnosis methods were manually interpreted from cardiotocography data which leads to subjective or erroneous decisions. With the help of Machine learning and accessing cardiotocography data (CTG) it provides some crucial advantages for identification of different fetal physiological states (Normal, Suspected and Pathological) by analyzing different fetal heart rate patterns and provide accurate observations. Analyzing various health parameters, including physiological indicators and factors a elaborate dataset has been utilized to train and evaluate supervised machine learning models. KNN, random forest, logistic regression, decision trees, neural network and gradient boosting has been employed to optimize predictive accuracy. The paper encompasses rigorous preprocessing steps, machine learning algorithm performance and evaluation metrics. Results demonstrate the effectiveness in early detection, providing a foundation for proactive healthcare, diagnostic accuracy, improves maternal-fetal outcomes while addressing issues such as data imbalance and interpretability. Future advancement focuses real time analysis, IOT integration which will bridge the gap between clinical implementation and adoption.

articleTitle: Virtual Reality Meets AI: Revolutionizing Physical Education with LiDAR and RL
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Physical education (PE) is changing as a result of the incorporation of cutting-edge technology like LiDAR, virtual reality (VR), and reinforcement learning (RL). The shortcomings of subjective evaluations and environmental restrictions in conventional physical education methods are addressed by these technologies, delivering accurate motion tracking, real-time feedback, and personalised learning.As a way to improve safety, engagement, and inclusion in physical education, it is necessary to improve motion capture accuracy, optimise abilities using RL, and offer immersive feedback through VR.RL algorithms optimized movement patterns, LiDAR sensors captured 3D motion data, and VR settings provided realistic feedback. With biomechanical analysis to predict the likelihood of injuries and Kalman filtering for data smoothing, the necessary accurate real-time feedback on corrections was generated. This solution increased engagement by 25.8%, injury detection by 34.9%, feedback efficiency by 31.2%, and tracking accuracy by 27.2%. The technique emerged as a good option in motion analysis and augmentation for learning purposes, compared with conventional techniques and other highly advanced technologies. This LiDAR, RL, and VR integration redefine PE in such a way that promises real motion tracking, adaptive feedback and safety. It has got enormous potential for upgrading physical education methods with encouragement for variety and participation.

articleTitle: Understanding the Landscape of Electric Vehicle Charging: A Multi-Dimensional Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: One of the most prominent strides towards sustainable transportation with decreasing greenhouse gas emissions involves a transition to electric vehicles, also known as EVs. This paper is meant to give an in-depth view of the different EV charging technologies: Level 1, Level 2, and DC fast charging; along with their implications regarding infrastructure development, user experience, and grid integration. A multi-dimensional analysis of the charging solutions evaluates the performance, efficiency, cost-effectiveness, and environmental impacts. Moreover, this research work identifies the role of charging networks and government policies besides consumer behavior in shaping the EV charging landscape. This paper tries to identify major challenges and opportunities in the present charging ecosystem through qualitative and quantitative approaches of methods and insights toward stakeholders in order to improve the adoption and integration of electric vehicles in urban and rural spaces.

articleTitle: Real Time Hand Gesture Recognition Using LSTM Based Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This research introduces a cutting-edge system for real-time hand gesture recognition using deep learning techniques. Gesture recognition is a vital technology that can enhance numerous applications, including sign language translation, secure communications, and various healthcare services.
