In this methodology, implementation of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, a specialized type of Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) is observed, which is well suited for sequential data analysis. Initially, the captured dataset undergoes data augmentation. The proposed system operates by capturing live video feeds to extract essential key points from hand movements, which are then analyzed to recognize specific gestures through a sophisticated deep-learning algorithm. By concentrating on the spatial and temporal dynamics of hand movements, this approach significantly improves both accuracy and responsiveness in real-time interactions. The overarching aim of this project is to facilitate effective communication between children who are deaf and mute and their parents or caregivers. By encouraging the learning and use of sign language, this gesture recognition system aims to enhance social interaction for these children. Furthermore, the system functions as an intermediary, seamlessly converting sign language gestures into spoken or written text in real-time. The proposed method demonstrates exceptional performance, achieving an accuracy of 99.6%. The results validate the robustness of the implemented techniques and suggest that the methodology could be highly beneficial for real-world applications.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity for Industrial IoT: A Review on Vulnerabilities and Attacks
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Internet has evolved from a network of connecting people to a network of connecting things, leading to a more complex and sophisticated network of Industrial Things, known as Industrial IoT (IIoT) today. This evolution has revolutionized the traditional Industrial system into real-time smarter systems that enhanced overall efficiency and productivity. Despite its benefits, the interconnected nature of IIoT, expanded the attack surface, exposing the systems to new crucial and complex cybersecurity threats. Several real time attacks on various industries as mentioned in this paper and the increasing cybersecurity cost over the years, clearly states the need of robust security solutions. To deeply understand the cybersecurity aspect, we provided a comprehensive study of attacks and vulnerabilities in this paper. In this paper, we did a indepth study of various IIoT related severe attacks and aspects related to these attacks, like vulnerabilities, impacts, potential solutions etc. We also provided future research directions to help the research community, to work upon and develop more robust and efficient cybersecurity solutions.

articleTitle: Advanced Course Equivalence Certification Using NLP Technology through Word Mover's Distance in Global Academic Credit Transfers
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: As the competition for higher education and professional employment intensifies globally, the proper evaluation and translation of academic credits and qualification systems has taken on a key significance. Most classic techniques for evaluating the contents of equivalence course certificates, such as Jaccard Index or Cosine, are too simplistic and do not reveal differences in educational credentials or course materials that are found at a semantically deeper structure. These techniques are primarily based on the surface-level characteristics of the texts, ignoring their inherent pictures. To overcome these challenges, this paper considers the possibility of using methods of Natural Language Processing (NLP), especially Word Mover's Distance, in the context of higher education and professional qualification, academic credit and course equivalency evaluation. WMD, or Word Mover's Distance, is a more sophisticated method of NLP, which describes the food transport distance problem and searches for the optimal distance between two different documents. The advantages of this methodology lie in comparing the course description and qualifications from a different perspective without losing the true meaning of these words in relation to course equivalence certificate comparison. On the basis of our study, we can state that WMD implements better than other conventional approaches and is an appealing solution for credit system transfer, the degree equivalence process evaluation in higher education, and employment clearance services. In this way, WMD applications for NLP purposes will allow for the sustainable recognition of the international qualifications of professionals and students, thus enhancing their movement across borders.

articleTitle: A Dual Machine Learning Approach for Differentiating Spindle Cell and Giant Cell Carcinomas and Assessing Severity Levels
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Lung cancer is a major health challenge throughout the world, there is an urgent need for innovative method for detection and diagnosis. This paper introduced a dual machine learning framework to improve the diagnosis and treatment guidelines. Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers is utilized to analysis of patient history, obtained accuracy of 92.5%, showing deep context understanding of Medicals chronicle. And also Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) was utilized to differentiate between Gait cell carcinoma and spindle cell carcinoma and achieved the accuracy of 94.2% and 93.7% respectively. High performance metrics like AUC, ROC ranging from 97% for both carcinoma types. These findings demonstrated a more precise method for lung cancer diagnosis and suitable treatment planning.

articleTitle: Optimizing GNSS Receiver Software for Enhanced Signal Processing Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) are essential for contemporary applications involving timing, navigation, and positioning. With an emphasis on the navigation processing session—where signals acquired from satellites are converted into user position, velocity, and time information—this study focuses on designing and implementing a software-based GNSS receiver. Signal acquisition, tracking, and processing of navigation data are the three main phases of GNSS receiver operation. To ensure dependable satellite signal reception, signal acquisition and tracking are crucial. However, this study goes deeper into the navigation session, which includes position estimate techniques, decoding navigation messages, and computing pseudo-range measurements. Advanced methods including extended Kalman filtering and least-squares placement are incorporated into the navigation module to improve accuracy and dependability in difficult situations, such as signal-rich areas and urban canyons. Through the development of an adaptable software architecture, the receiver may handle several GNSS constellations, such as BeiDou, GPS, Galileo, and GLONASS. Modularity, scalability, and interoperability with a wide range of applications—from autonomous navigation to geospatial mapping—are given top priority in the system architecture. The software's ability to achieve sub-meter-level positioning precision is demonstrated through performance validation utilizing both simulated and real-world GNSS data. By highlighting the significance of the navigation session and offering creative methods for reliable and accurate position determination in a variety of operational settings, this work advances GNSS receiver technology.

articleTitle: Satellite Image Segmentation using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This paper offers a deep learning approach for semantic satellite imagery segmentation utilizing a modified U-Net architecture. Leveraging a Dubai satellite imagery dataset, the model classifies six distinct land-use categories, including buildings, roads, vegetation, and water bodies. Preprocessing methods including patch creation, normalization, and class balance are incorporated into the implementation through augmenting data. Combining categorical focal loss and dice loss, which addresses class imbalance and improves segmentation accuracy, is one of the major advances. The study demonstrates the model's robustness in different fields of environmental monitoring and urban planning applications. Insights into spatial resolution challenges and model optimization strategies are also discussed.

articleTitle: CGDeepAff: Deep Learning-Based Approach for Protein-Ligand Binding Affinity Estimation Using CNN-GRU
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Protein-ligand binding affinity prediction is one of the most important phases in drug development since it directs the selection and optimization of therapeutic molecules. We introduce CGDeepAff, a unique deep-learning framework that combines CNNs and Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) to estimate protein-ligand binding affinities accurately. This model incorporates various features to improve prediction accuracy, including numerical data, amino acid counts (aa counts), and protein sequences. On the CASF-2016 benchmark dataset, CGDeepAff surpasses previous models with Spearman's <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho$</tex> of 0.861, Pearson's <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> of 0.855, and RMSE of 1.002. Finally, when compared to models like HAC-Net <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R=0.846, \rho=0.843$</tex>, RMSE = 1.205) and K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DEEP</inf> <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R=0.82, \rho=0.82$</tex>, RMSE = 1.27), CGDeepAff outperforms them, especially in treating various protein-ligand complexes. These results indicate that CGDeepAff is a broadly generalizable method capable of being used in computational drug discovery. Thus, CGDeepAff constitutes a further step forward in the binding affinity prediction, possibly leading to a better tool for drug discovery.

articleTitle: AI-Pollinators for Blueberry Farming: Enhancing Cross-Pollination Efficiency Through Autonomous Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This research work presents an AI-based system to enhance blueberry pollination in consideration of the dwindling numbers of pollinating insects, which selects the mature flowers that are ready for pollination. Detecting and classifying blueberry flowers as “Immature” or “Mature” using YOLOv11n model, the system identifies matured flowers using real-time image recognition to guide robotic arms or drones for accurate, precise and targeted pollination. The complex structure of blueberry flowers with reproductive parts that are hidden makes it quite difficult to detect blueberry flowers; however, the augmentation of this dataset definitely resulted in significant improvement in model accuracy. The final model proved effective performance along with tremendous mean Average Precision scores and efficient inference times that warrant real-world deployment. This approach is highly scalable and sustainable in agriculture, adding yield by maximizing pollination approaches and reducing relevance on labor and numbers of dwindling bee populations in the environment. Future work intends collecting further dataset and understanding advanced imaging techniques to improve detection accuracy so as to position this system as a potential tool for precision agriculture.

articleTitle: Design of a High-Efficiency Class-AB RF Power Amplifier for 3.7–4.2 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Power amplifiers are important in today's wireless communication systems. This paper describes the design, tuning, and performance optimization of a class-AB power amplifier operating in the 3.7 GHz – 4.2 GHz frequency range with an output power of 40 dBm at a gain of about 10 dB. A Wolfspeed CGH40010F GaN HEMT transistor, which operates from DC with a 28V supply, is employed in the amplifier's design to satisfy the specifications. Using the transistor nonlinear simulation model created by Cree Inc., an amplifier is designed and simulated in Keysight Advanced Design System (ADS) software. Keeping the issues of linearity and efficiency in mind, the biasing point is chosen for the class AB configuration. In biasing, the drain current is 48 mA and the gate-source voltage is −3.05 V. The frequency range for the design is chosen based on applications. Then, the stability analysis of the transistor is performed. The simulation results also show that the transistor becomes broadband stable when a resistor is added to its input side. Source-pull and load-pull simulation is used to extract source and load impedances for optimal power and efficiency. From the perspectives of efficiency and linearity, the installed PA performs exceptionally well across the entire frequency range. According to the simulation, the RF PA's flat gain fluctuated between 8.19 dB and 10.90 dB for the frequency range of 3.7 GHz to 4.2 GHz. At 3.8 GHz, the maximum power added efficiency (PAE) was found to be 64.52%, while the maximum drain efficiency is simulated to reach 67.78% at an output power of nearly 40 dBm.

articleTitle: Current Trends on Limited View CT Reconstruction Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Image reconstruction is at the core of improving Computed Tomography (CT), enabling high-quality imaging while addressing challenges like noise, limited data, and radiation exposure. Recent innovations have introduced adaptive algorithms that enhance reconstruction efficiency, clarity, and safety, making CT more effective in diverse applications. The Parameter-extended Expectation-Maximization (PXEM) algorithm dynamically adjusts reconstruction parameters during iterations, demonstrating superior noise resilience and faster convergence, especially in high-noise environments. Similarly, the Simultaneous Algebraic Reconstruction Technique with Guided Filtering (SART-G) uses prior guidance images to retain structural details and outperform traditional methods, such as Filtered Back Projection (FBP) and standard SART, in low-exposure and limited-projection scenarios. Muon Computed Tomography (MCT) presents a novel, non-invasive approach that utilizes cosmic-ray muons for imaging dense and complex materials. MCT has significant potential in nuclear safety and industrial applications where conventional CT faces limitations. Meanwhile, the Simultaneous Algebraic Reconstruction Technique with Total Variation (SART-TV) mitigates noise accumulation in sparse-angle imaging by applying total variation regularization, ensuring enhanced image quality while minimizing radiation exposure. These advancements illustrate the transformative impact of modern image reconstruction algorithms on CT technology. By integrating adaptive noise reduction, efficient data utilization, and safety-oriented approaches, these methods pave the way for more precise and versatile CT applications in clinical, research, and industrial settings. This article presents an overview of some of the CT reconstruction iterative techniques that are commonly used in CT reconstruction from limited views.

Author Keywords: Simultaneous Algebraic Reconstruction Technique with Guided Filtering (SART-G)
Simultaneous Algebraic Reconstruction Technique with Total Variation (SART-TV)

articleTitle: Designing and Implementing an IoT-Based Long-Distance Fire-Extinguishment System “Stationary 3-Axis Fire-Emergency Response Base”
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of an Internet of Thing (IOT)-based long-distance fire-extinguishment system named “Stationary 3-Axis Fire-Emergency Response Base” (STAFERB). The system aims to provide immediate response to fire hazards in various environments, including residential areas, building complexes, commercial areas, small-scale industries, large factories, dense slum areas, and remotely located forest regions. The proposed STAFERB is designed to receive fire location coordinates, fire intensity, and probable cause information. It then calculates the path of a projectile based on considering obstacles and self-detection of a clear line of sight to reach the t1arget location. The system uses this information to select the appropriate speed and type of fire retardant. The designed STAFERB features robust communication, self-path detection, auto-orientation, and reduced response time, making it a significant advancement in fire-fighting technology. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed STAFERB in mitigating fire hazards and hence can be well suited for real-time disaster management.

articleTitle: Under Water Localization and Mapping Integrated with Object Detection Classification and LIDAR Sensing Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This research aims at exploring the fused subaqueous concurrent localization and mapping with LiDAR sensing for enhanced immediate mapping for the underwater terrain. By integrating distance measurements from LiDAR and dynamic localization, this approach provides better accuracy and solution time in exploring submerged terrains like seafloors, aquatic vegetables and man-made structures. These technologies extend the capabilities of AUVs and ROVs with continuous and accurate mapping and navigation facilities especially in GPS dead-reckoning environments. This research has important possibilities for revolutionizing the collection of underwater data in many sectors such as oceanography, environmental protection, and resource management. The progress ion of these techniques will further the interests of industries through more efficient exploratory, preservation, and construction processes in aquatic contexts.

articleTitle: Improving Early Cardiomyopathy Diagnosis with CNNs: A Deep Learning-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Cardiomyopathy is the type of heart disease that results from diabetes that influences the heart muscles, leading to structural and functional abnormalities and these situations can weaken the heart muscle, loss its ability to supply blood effectively. Cardiomyopathy affects millions worldwide every year, with an estimated 1 in 500 people impacted. In the United States, it leads to approximately 50,000 deaths are reported annually. The existing method with Logistic Regression for the detection of Cardiomyopathy obtained inaccurate results with a high false alarm rate. Introduced a deep leaning convolution neural networks algorithm for the preprocessing, extraction of data selection of features and diagnosis of disease with accurate results in the early stage. As a result, got the accurate performance for accuracy, precision, sensitivity, and recall with 97%, 96%, 95.6%, and 96% respectively.

articleTitle: AgriTalk: Revolutionizing Farming with a Multilingual Chatbot
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Agriculture plays a vital role in the economy of many nations, especially in regions where a significant portion of the population depends on it for their livelihood. Despite its importance, linguistic and technological barriers often hinder access to accurate agricultural information. This article introduces a multilingual chatbot designed to address agricultural queries efficiently. Leveraging Natural Language Processing and deep learning models, this multi-language chatbot accommodates English, Hindi, Malayalam, Kannada, and Telugu. Since the query is matched with relevant responses using cosine similarity on the sentence-transformers architecture, the system ensures that relevant responses are given. With IndicTrans2 (AI4Bharat), a robust neural machine translation model tailored for Indian languages, the facility provides a single-machine foundation on which translations about 22 Indian languages with subsequent additional features-text-to-speech functionality enhances accessibility to varied users. The system design, data preprocessing, implementation, and evaluation metrics are covered in this study, which also shows how it might help farmers and other agricultural stakeholders.

articleTitle: Leveraging Gait Patterns and Machine Learning for Early Detection of Alzheimer's Disease
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Alzheimer's Disease (AD), a leading cause of dementia, is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder. Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) serves as a transitional phase between cognitive normality (CN) and AD. Gait analysis has emerged as a promising non-invasive diagnostic tool for detecting early stages of MCI and AD. This study analyzed gait and cognitive assessments from 102 participants divided into AD (n = 27), MCI (n = 35), and Normal Control (NC; n = 40) groups, using single-task and dual-task gait paradigms. Machine learning (ML) models were developed to classify cognitive states, without Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Random Forest achieved 87% accuracy, and LSTM reached 95% for dual-task data. Incorporating PCA improved performance, with Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Linear SVC achieving 100% accuracy for single-task data, while for dual-task data, Random Forest and LSTM achieved 91% and 99% accuracy, respectively. These experimental findings highlight the potential use of ML-based gait analysis as an effective tool for early detection of AD and MCI, offering opportunities for timely intervention and management.

articleTitle: Optimizing Early Detection of Lung Disease Through Data-Driven Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Lung illness is any condition that impairs the lungs' capacity to function normally; diabetes, in particular, can have a variety of effects on the lungs and increases the risk of respiratory infections such as pneumonia and TB in those who have it. According to recent studies, 384 million individuals have chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and 3 million of them pass away each year as a result of delayed diagnosis. Early detection of any disease can lessen its severity, which will lower the death rate and number of lung disease sufferers. Used deep learning methods for lung detection diagnostics, such as improved fish bee (IFB) and chaotic bird swam optimization (CBSO), despite the prediction rate's high false rate and lack of accuracy. Introduced a technique using machine learning methods, such as the Principal Component Analysis (PCA) algorithm for extraction of features, the Decision Tree approach for sample categorization, and the Support Vector Machine (SVM) for very accurate early illness diagnosis. The results of the suggested approach for early lung tumor identification with a low incorrect rate showed an accuracy of 98.07.

articleTitle: Data Sampling Methods for Predicting CKD and Diabetes with Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The exponential expansion of data generation in the internet age has had a major impact on a number of sectors, including medical exploration. still, handling unstable datasets is one of the difficulties faced by experimenters in the field of drug. This problem occurs when there's an unstable distribution of classes in a dataset, which could lead to one class being mainly more multitudinous than the others. The creation of precise individual models can be seriously hampered by imbalanced datasets. In this design, we concentrate on two medical datasets the PIMA INDIAN DIABETICS dataset and the habitual order complaint dataset. Experimenters have been probing a number of styles to balance the datasets previous to training machine literacy models in order to overcome this difficulty. Data about people's health characteristics, similar as blood pressure, blood sugar, and other material clinical pointers, are included in these databases. The quantum of data generated is growing snappily in the period of the internet. Research in medical supplementary opinion is decreasingly being backed by artificial intelligence, especially big data categorization technologies. still, because sample crops differ, medical big data constantly has imbalances. In general, the term “imbalanced data” describes a situation where several data samples within a specific problem are not distributed unevenly, which results in one or further classes in the dataset being underrepresented. Traditional bracket ways generally assume that training misclassification costs are the same for all classes and that each class has an analogous quantum of samples.

articleTitle: Deploying UAV's Equipped with LIDAR for the Quantification of Tree Biomass and the Systematic Classification of Arboreal Species
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Research was like looking deep into the use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) as platforms to carry light detection and ranging (LiDAR) systems, essentially applied ostensibly for precise biomass measurements of trees and systematic classification of tree species and other purposes. By capturing high-density point cloud data, the study is able to undertake a comprehensive assessment of forests of their not only structural attributes but also spatial attributes. The UAVs will fly predefined paths so that they can record data across the widest areas and through the most different terrain with minimum interference from human contact. The LiDAR data collected are subjected to advanced preprocessing techniques like outlier removal and noise reduction for improved fidelity measures. Each tree species is classified with computational engines using morphological and radiometric features for the accurate differentiation of the taxa. Simultaneously, biomass estimation is done with very high accuracy, demonstrating the capability of the system to manage complex forested environments. It stresses the transformational aspect of UAV-LiDAR systems in ecological monitoring and their contribution to sustainable forest management through powerful means of measurements and species identification. The advancement to environmental science occurs within the scope of promoting biodiversity conservation and re-invention of assessment methodologies for forestry resources.

articleTitle: Long Term Load Forecasting Using Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Electrical load forecasting is an vital module of power system planning and operation because accurate predictions regarding future electricity demand are imperative in the efficient management of resources and ensuring the reliability and stability of the power grid. Long-term load forecasting using machine learning approaches like ANNs in MATLAB offers effective resource management and maintaining reliability of the grid. Based on a historical load demand data set of 8,867 points, with a 24-hour lag feature to take care of temporal fluctuations, the study utilized an ANN model having 20 hidden layers and optimized it for both accuracy and computational efficiency. Three training algorithms were evaluated to check the convergence, accuracy, and generalization by Levenberg-Marquardt, Scaled Conjugate Gradient, and Bayesian Regulation. Results directed to identification of the appropriate algorithm that enhances energy distribution and management.

articleTitle: Automated Crop Disease Detection Using Deep Learning: A Scalable Smart Farming Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The maintenance of agricultural productivity depends on early detection of crop diseases, and traditional methods rely on plant pathology expertise, which can be resource-intensive. To address this, we propose an automated system using high-resolution images captured by drones and advanced deep learning architectures. The system uses a three-step classification approach: crop classification, disease detection, and disease classification. The drone technology allows for large-scale crop monitoring, and the architecture incorporates Vision Transformers for global feature extraction and EfficientNet-B0 for localized disease identification, ensuring robust performance. The addition of an “unknown” category improves generalization to unseen crops and diseases. This framework offers scalable, efficient disease detection, with significant potential for smart farming applications, especially in Solanaceae crops, and can be expanded to other agricultural settings.

articleTitle: Effect of Fiber Stacking Sequence and Nano-Graphene in Jute/Kenaf/Glass Hybrid Composite
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Natural resource fiber and synthetic fibers have become increasingly appealing to the automobile industry for sustainable use materials. These include augmenting mechanical strength, low density, effective thermal and acoustic insulation, and cost-effectiveness. Depending on specific needs, different types of fiber composites, such as natural, synthetic, or combinations of both, can be used for reinforcement. This study involved the samples of 20 different hybrid nanocomposites with varying sequences of fiber layers (glass fiber, jute fiber, and kenaf fiber), contributions Nanographene (3 wt%, 4wt%, and 5wt %), and orientations of fiber (0°. 45°.and 90°). Samples were prepared by compression molding technique and analyzed by response surface methodology (RSM) was used to maximize the tensile strength and impact strength. It was noticed that the sequences 1 in both mechanical properties, particularly with 5% Nano graphene filler with 90° fiber orientation exhibited the higher Tensile strength of 264 MPa and Impact strength of 91 kJ/m2. The models were statistically verified and validated and found accurate.

articleTitle: Exploring Reinforcement Learning in Autonomous Robot Path Planning and Obstacle Navigation
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The article deals with issues concerning the au-tonomous planning of trajectories and avoiding obstacles for mobile robots using reinforcement learning. The emphasis is on dynamic tasks performed by robots devoid of any prior knowledge or maps of the operating environment. In those conditions, conventional motion planning techniques do not work; however, Deep Reinforce-ment Learning (DRL) is a solution. DRL allows robots to learn and adapt independently while operating in real-time without human intervention, even in the most complicated environments. The research investigates different approaches including Q-learning, SARSA, and DQN algorithms, aiming to evaluate their differences based on the path length and the computational time in reaching that path. The findings confirm that DQN salvages SARSA and Q-learning in terms of efficiency and path optimization. The main focus of the research paper is the fusion of deep learning and reinforcement learning that enables the processing of the sensor to decision making, which in turn enhances the ability of the robot to navigate. The results of the experiments support the applicability of these methods in dynamic scenarios.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis Using LSTM Model for Emotion Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This research focuses on the role of Natural Language Processing in extracting, analysing, and interpreting textual data to identify sentiment and emotional patterns from tweets. NLP techniques, particularly deep learning techniques such as LSTM, allow for processing large-scale unstructured data while capturing contextual relationships within the text. The results of this study contribute to the NLP analysis and a wider area of mood, and understand the emotional tone of politicians and the perception of the general public. These results emphasize the importance of deep training models that have advanced in the analysis of political discourse, and this work is a social network researcher that tries to control and understand public mood in real time. In this study, we investigate the use of long -term data in memory networks to analyse the mood of the US President Donald Trump and Joe Biden. The study uses a dataset of over one million tweets and employs advanced natural language processing techniques such as text pre-processing, tokenization, and word embeddings to classify sentiment into positive, negative, or neutral categories. LSTM has the ability to capture long-term dependencies in sequential data and effectively resolves the complexities of informal, context-rich language in social networks. The proposed model achieved good accuracy and demonstrated its robustness in handling large-scale unstructured data.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Anaemia Detection: Leveraging Eye Condition Data and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Anemia, which is characterized by a low level of hemoglobin in the blood, can cause major damage to vital organs including the heart and kidneys. As per the records of 2021, 1.92 billion people are effected globally with anemia. Traditional diagnostic methods sometimes include invasive procedures, which makes patients anxious and delays treatment. This study offers a novel, non-invasive technique for identifying anemia by using pictures of the palpebral conjunctiva, which is known to exhibit pallor in anemic individuals. Our strategy is to offer a simple method for early identification of at-risk individuals by conjunctival paleness measurement, enabling timely interventions. Our novel approach ensures a rapid, simple, and accessible diagnosis of anemia for everyone by utilizing machine learning and integrating data on eye conditions. This technological breakthrough has the power to improve patient outcomes, enhance mental health globally, and alter the way healthcare is provided. We think that with more research and development, our approach will significantly impact the diagnosis of anemia and pave the way for better health outcomes everywhere.

articleTitle: IoT Device for Food Storage
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The integration of IoT technology provides realtime, data-driven monitoring that reduces waste and maintains the quality of the food, changing the way food is preserved and managed. This research focuses on the development and implementation of an Arduino-based IoT device for monitoring freshness, temperature, and humidity in storage food environments. Equipped with an MQ-4 methane sensor and DHT11 sensor, the system detects spoilage indicators and environmental conditions and opens an exhaust fan if the moisture has been in excess. The BLYNK IoT app provides instant information to the user about storage conditions, thus ensuring efficient and proactive food management. This product finds answers to some of the main food-related storage challenges by offering scalable and effective solutions for enhanced freshness and reduced spoilage.

articleTitle: UAV-Driven Surveillance: Security Enhancement with ML and Edge Detection Integrating LIDAR Sensor for Trespassing and Area Mapping
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This study investigates the integration of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) in security and surveillance systems to enhance countering trespassing and security measures. The study highlights the use of edge detection techniques, object detection, classification methods, and LIDAR data to improve UAV capabilities in monitoring and securing extensive and intricate areas. UAVs utilize edge detection to accurately identify boundaries, structures, and potential intruders, facilitating the definition of restricted zones and unauthorized activity detection. Furthermore, object detection and classification enable UAVs to distinguish between trespassers, vehicles, and other relevant objects, thereby enhancing decision-making and real-time alert systems. LIDAR data provides precise 3D reconstructions of the targeted region, aiding in both security monitoring and identifying environmental changes indicative of a breach. Machine learning models continuously improve detection accuracy and efficiency, allowing UAVs to adapt to dynamic environments with minimal human intervention. The integration of UAVs with these technologies offers a robust system for autonomous trespasser detection, area mapping, and rapid response to security threats. The findings underscore the scalability and efficiency of UAV-LIDAR integration as a solution for automated spatial analysis and strategic decision-making in remote, dynamic, and high-stakes environments.

articleTitle: Maximizing Productivity: Leveraging Existing Resources and Advanced Technologies for Automation and Prompt Engineering
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This study explores automation and prompt engineering to enhance productivity by leveraging both emerging and existing technologies. It covers topics such as automated bug fixing, AI-driven office tasks, web data extraction, smart homes, and the evolving workplace. Practical examples using Linux and Python are provided, emphasizing how even small-scale automation projects can have a significant impact. The study also highlights the importance of effective communication with automated systems and shares research insights and real-world experiences to help users optimize automation techniques for various applications.

articleTitle: A Review of Integrated Advancements in Waste Detection in Marine Environments Using Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Garbage and waste disposal pose significant challenges for sustainability, necessitating effective recycling and waste management systems in any sustainable community. Among these issues, marine debris-comprising floating or submerged waste-represents a severe environmental threat in coastal regions. Submerged debris, which often includes recyclable materials like plastics, metals, and glass, can persist in aquatic ecosystems for decades, jeopardizing both environmental and human health. This review examines the use of advanced object detection techniques, including YOLOv4, YOLOv5 and other methodologies, for identifying marine debris in SONAR imagery. By evaluating the performance and accuracy of these detection methods, this paper seeks to advance the development of efficient solutions for marine debris management, ultimately promoting environmental sustainability and safeguarding public health.

articleTitle: Grid-Integrated Solar Power: A Conclusive Review on Technologies, Challenges, and Strategies
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The incorporation of solar electricity into the electrical grid is a growing field of study, motivated by the imperative to diminish carbon emissions and fulfil the rising requirement for sustainable energy sources. This review examines the current advances in grid-integrated solar power systems, with a specific emphasis on photovoltaic and solar thermal technology. The technology tackles issues such as the fluctuation of solar energy, the stability of the power grid, and the quality of power, providing innovative approaches and considering economic and regulatory factors. The study provides energy stakeholders, academics, engineers, and policymakers with the essential knowledge required to shift towards a sustainable and resilient energy system.

articleTitle: A Brief Review on Photocatalytic Materials for Waste Water Treatment
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The escalating contamination of wastewater by toxic pollutants from domestic, commercial, and industrial sources poses significant threats to global water security, food safety, and marine ecosystems. Conventional wastewater treatment methods often fail to address persistent organic pollutants, including dyes, pesticides, and endocrine disruptors, necessitating advanced solutions for sustainable environmental management. This work comprehensively focuses on photocatalysis as a cutting-edge advanced oxidation process (AOP) for the efficient degradation of recalcitrant contaminants in industrial wastewater. The process focused on the mechanisms of hydroxyl radical (•OH) formation through light-driven catalytic reactions. The study also evaluates the efficacy of various metal-oxide semiconductor nanomaterials here. The research further explores advancements such as doping strategies, hybrid nanocomposites, and reactor design innovations to overcome challenges like electron-hole recombination, toxic byproduct formation, and scalability. This work also highlights the potential of engineered photocatalytic systems to achieve near-complete mineralization of pollutants into harmless byproducts, offering a cost-effective and environmentally sustainable alternative to traditional methods. The study concludes with actionable insights for optimizing photocatalytic efficiency under solar irradiation, aligning with global efforts to achieve UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) for clean water and ecosystem preservation.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Planar and Conformal Meta-Surfaces in the Design of Multiband Array Antennas: Challenges and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This paper provides a detailed review of planar and conformal meta-surface designs for multi-band array antennas, highlighting their role in modern wireless communication and radar systems. Meta-surfaces, with their ability to accurately manipulate electromagnetic wave propagation, has revolutionized antenna design by enabling enhanced functionalities such as beam steering, polarization control, and frequency reconfiguration. Planar meta-surfaces excel in simplicity, scalability, and high gain for planar-surface applications, while conformal meta-surfaces offer adaptability to curved geometries, making them ideal for wearable and aerospace applications.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Early Prediction of Pulmonary Fibrosis Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The development of scar tissue (fibrosis) in the lungs is a hallmark of pulmonary fibrosis, a progressive lung disease. impairing its ability to function properly. Progressive nature leading to declining lung function and yearly, 13 to 20 out of 100,00 people effecting by pulmonary fibrosis throughout the world. Present technologies for prediction of pulmonary fibrosis are limited to predictive accuracy, availability of high-quality data and early detection. The recommended technique with a high-resolution computed Tomography (HRCT) scan along with U-Net for better classification of HRCT signals and diagnosis of disease accurately. The results accomplished by this method are remarkable achievements in terms of precision recall, accuracy and F1-Score ranging from 0.96 to 0.98.

articleTitle: A Review: How Employed Word Embeddings in Paraphrase Detection?
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: A journey through the evolution of word embeddings from their humble beginnings to the techniques of the highest standard in paraphrase detection explain the advantages of using such specific models like Word2Vec and GloVe, which have revolutionized how machines understand human language. Along the way, challenges encountered by these methods such as dealing with bias and handling contextual nuances and adapting pre-trained embeddings to specific domains or tasks. Often requiring significant fine-tuning or domain-specific training. There is a need for more efficient methods to adapt general-purpose embeddings to specialized domains without losing their broad applicability. Exploring meta-learning approaches or developing more sophisticated fine-tuning techniques could enhance domain adaptation capabilities. Temporal dynamics in word embeddings of most current embedding models provide static representations that do not account for how word meanings and relationships evolve over time. There is limited research on creating dynamic word embeddings that can capture temporal shifts in language use and meaning. This paper describes potential future developments in the field, where context-aware embeddings and multi-modal representations promise to further bridge the gap between humans and machines. This comprehensive review serves as both a map and a compass for researchers navigating the complex terrain of word embeddings in paraphrase detection under NLP.

articleTitle: Gen AI lens: Precision Diagnostics Through Interactive Segmentation and User centric Innovation in Medical Imaging
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence has brought transformative advancements to medical imaging, improving diagnostic precision and enabling clinicians to interact more effectively with advanced tools. This research highlights the role of generative AI in interactive segmentation techniques, which allow precise identification of anatomical structures and pathological conditions. By leveraging deep learning, generative models enhance segmentation accuracy, facilitate timely and accurate diagnoses. Despite these advancements, significant challenges remain, like the need for large, annotated datasets, the risk of algorithmic bias, and the complexities of integrating AI systems into existing workflows. The study emphasizes the importance of intuitive interfaces that empower clinicians to utilize AI-driven tools effectively. Looking ahead, future efforts should focus on developing robust models that generalize across diverse populations and integrating patient-specific data to enable personalized diagnostics. While generative AI has immense potential to revolutionize medical imaging and improve healthcare outcomes, addressing these challenges is essential to fully realize its benefits.

articleTitle: The Advancements of Autonomous Robotic Surgery: A Path Towards Fully Automated Procedures
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Autonomous robotic surgery stands at the leading edge of a revolution in healthcare where robots, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and advanced imaging promise to perform many surgical procedures with minimal direct human intervention. The potential of such systems is even in the poorest areas to augment access to professional care, to reduce recovery time, and increase precision. They are minimally invasive technologies which are designed to maximize treatment results with minimum errors. However, fully automated surgery is a challenge that requires adaptive decision-making, sophisticated sensory feedback, and the ability to overcome technical constraints. Adoption is further complicated by changing regulatory frameworks and ethical issues like patient consent and data protection. Economic constraints are caused by high development and implementation expenses. This study examines the potential for autonomous robotic surgery to revolutionize healthcare by reviewing recent research and clinical data. It presents the latest developments, key challenges, and potential future developments and, hence, provides an exhaustive overview of the merits and demerits of this technology in relation to changing the nature of surgical care.

articleTitle: The Convergence of Cognitive Radio and 6G: Opportunities, Applications, and Technical Considerations
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The emergence of 6G technology holds great potential to transform wireless communications by providing un-precedented communication and computation speeds, extremely low latency, and sustainable connections. In order to use the features of the 6G networks, cognitive radio (CR) technology, which has the capacity to dynamically access the spectrum and adjust to network conditions, is expected to be essential. This paper explores the convergence of CR and 6G, highlighting the opportunities this synergy presents, potential applications, and the technical considerations that must be addressed. In addition, it discusses how CR can improve spectrum efficiency, improve network resilience, and enable novel use cases in 6G. In addition, the challenges in implementing CR in 6G networks are examined, including issues related to security, energy efficiency, and computational complexity. In order to realize the promise of CR in 6G networks, important research topics and offers insight into the future direction of wireless communication are also analyzed and presented.

articleTitle: Leveraging UAV-Mounted LIDAR Technology for Three-Dimensional Mapping and Cartographic Assessment of Uninhabited Terrains
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Lidar sensing and 3d mapping presents substantial benefits for enhancing security in abandoned and high risk areas. With laser pulses and analyzing the reflected signals LIDAR generates precise three dimensional model of terrain structures and any objects. These technology allows security teams to remotely access a sites detecting illegal activities or potential dangers without entering unsafe environments. The detailed mapping enables effective monitoring of access points, route planning and vulnrerabitiy identification, ensuring prompt response to threats. With high accuracy and real time data, LIDAR based 3D mapping significantly strengthens security operations, facilitating the protection of uninhabited locations. UAV mounted LIDAR technology further amplifies this capability by creating detailed accurate model of landscapes, including topography, vegetation and structures. This innovative method supports remote surveillance of detoriating sites, enabling enhanced threat and detection and the development of strategy security measures, improving safety and operational efficiency in areas with elevated risks.

articleTitle: A Subsequent Behavioral Study of Individuals and NLP Approach to Predict Their Personality
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The prime focus of this project is to sort people according to their Myers-Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI) personality type using NLP model and also conduct a comparative study of their behavior. We will be using individuals’ real-time text data that they type while using their personal computers as the main key figure of our analytical study. For the sake of better analysis, we will also go through the self-questionnaire test format of MBTI detection. Our text-based model will be able to operate on a large scale of data ensuring a strong linguistic basis for MBTI rather than the test taken where there is a slight probability that it will create different results on different scenarios.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Classification Using Deep Learning with Explainable AI (XAI)
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This paper presents a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based system for classifying brain tumor types using advanced deep learning techniques and Explainable AI (XAI). The system analyzes medical images to distinguish between four classes: Glioma, Meningioma, Pituitary, and No Tumor. The model was implemented using PyTorch. Established CNN architectures such as EfficientNet, MobileNet, and ResNet for robust performance. Training and testing were conducted on a dataset of approximately 3,000 images, with results demonstrating exceptional performance. The best-performing model, EfficientNet B1, achieved a training accuracy of 99.72% and a test accuracy of 99.43%, with a training loss of 0.0115 and a test loss of 0.0264. Explainable AI techniques were employed to enhance transparency and interpretability, providing insights into the decision-making process of the models. This integration of XAI ensures the system's reliability and usability in real-world medical applications. Furthermore, the entire system, including the trained models and XAI components, was successfully deployed, enabling practical use and further validation in clinical settings.

articleTitle: A Brief Review on AI Based Stock Market Prediction Tools
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The stock market has emerged as a recent trend in investment, particularly favored by the younger generation over traditional bank deposits like fixed deposits and savings accounts due to its lucrative returns. The advent of technology has made it easier to invest in stock markets and predict their returns. Artificial Intelligence, a newcomer to this field, has also enhanced the trustworthiness of stock market investments through algorithms such as Random Forest, SVM, RBFNN, WMA, and LSTM. Predicting stock market trends is crucial for global investors, and with technological advancements, AI algorithms have become an essential tool for analyzing data and making highly accurate predictions about stock movements or market trends. This work briefly discusses the current AI-based stock market analysis tools.

articleTitle: An Innovative Approach to Precise Localization Leveraging a Single Anchor Node
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: As such, this project aims at creating an efficient localization system to aid in the target trapping of unknown areas often caused by natural disasters and man-made human conflicts. Traditional navigation systems may be partially or fully unavailable in such scenarios. To that effect, we are looking at a single-anchor node localization scheme in the form of TSAL as a fallback when more conventionally oriented methods fail. TSAL relies on a mathematical model to predict the location of a mobile device with minimal reliance on multiple anchors. The system's performance is tested through simulations and real- world experiments in indoor, outdoor, and mixed environments. The most important metrics that are measured are localization accuracy, computational complexity, and robustness to signal interference. The results are compared to multi-anchor methods to present the advantages and limitations of the single-anchor scheme. TSAL is cost- effective, scalable, and appropriate for applications like indoor navigation, autonomous vehicles, and IoT systems where deploying multiple anchors is impractical. It decreases infrastructure costs with high accuracy while working in challenging environments. With the use of Cartesian coordinate systems and off-the-shelf measurements such as distance or steering angle, TSAL uses a single functioning cellular base station or redeployed station to locate the target. However, the scheme also supports a variant with TML, enhancing accuracy. The proposed schemes have been confirmed in terms of effectiveness and availability through intensive simulations, theoretical analyses, and real-world experiments.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Privacy and Security Implications of Mobile Apps
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The rapid growth of mobile applications, combined with an increasing reliance on these apps for a variety of purposes, has prompted serious concerns about user privacy and data security. This study aims to assess the privacy practices, data handling methods, and security vulnerabilities of mobile apps in a variety of categories, including social media, e-commerce, health and fitness, and financial management. This study identifies major privacy and security issues by examining privacy policies and terms of service, as well as how these apps handle sensitive data. The study also examines free and premium apps' privacy procedures, taking into account the implications for user data protection. The findings illustrate differences in data handling and security standards across different app categories, highlighting the importance of transparent privacy policies, strong security mechanisms, and limited data sharing to protect user information. The research helps to define standards and best practices for promoting secure app activity, increasing user confidence, and guaranteeing a safer digital environment.

articleTitle: Empowering Recommendations: Survey of LLM-Based Recommendation Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: The rise of e-commerce has emphasized the importance of recommendation systems in enhancing user experiences. Traditional methods, like collaborative filtering and content-based techniques, often struggle with understanding user preferences. Large Language Models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT and GPT-4, offer a transformative approach by leveraging advanced natural language processing. This survey explores LLM-driven strategies in recommendation systems, focusing on their role in feature encoding, user-item interaction modeling, and explainability. By highlighting their ability to generate contextually relevant recommendations, we provide insights into their advantages over conventional methods and their potential for future advancements.

articleTitle: Early Prediction of Alzheimer's Dementia Using Random Forest Machine Learning Algorithm: A Data-Driven Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Alzheimer's dementia is liberal neurological ailment categorized by memory loss, cerebral failure, and it is the utmost communal form of dementia and typically affects older adults. Every year, 6.7 million people are affecting by Alzheimer's dementia (AD) in USA and 4.3% probability of developing Alzheimer's ailment earlier the age of 65 in India. The principal issue associated with delayed prediction of Alzheimer's dementia lies in the incapacity to intervene during the formative years of the dementia progression, thereby missing opportunities for timely intervention and treatment. Available techniques for finding of Alzheimer's dementia with machine learning algorithms resulted in inability to predict the dementia early. For proactive diagnosis of Alzheimer's dementia, proposed a novel technique using Random Forest categorizer and also compared among various machine learning classifiers. Resulted in obtained accurate results with 97.5% of accuracy.

articleTitle: Ensemble Clustering on Big Data
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Ensemble clustering is a powerful technique that enhances cluster analysis by combining multiple algorithms. In the realm of big data, efficiently processing and analyzing large datasets remains a significant challenge. We introduce a novel clustering algorithm designed for big data environments, leveraging the MapReduce framework to integrate Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise and K-means algorithms. The proposed method first applies DBSCAN to remove noise and identify dense regions, K-means is then used to rectify clustering and extract meaningful insights. Implementing these steps within the MapReduce framework ensures efficient parallel processing and scalability. Prior research has employed K-means and DBSCAN for cluster analysis but has not profited from the MapReduce framework. Our approach demonstrates superior accuracy, the proposed method's effectiveness is underscored by the improved silhouette scores that have been observed. Results affirm that the integration of DBSCAN and K-means within MapReduce significantly enhances clustering performance for large-scale datasets.

articleTitle: Design of Chattering Free Sliding Mode Control Law for Trajectory Tracking of Quadcopters
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This research proposes new methods of controlling quadcopters utilising Sliding Mode Control (SMC) to provide accurate trajectory tracking with significant reduction in chattering. SMC is an effective control law for quadcopters as it can potentially deal with unanticipated parameter variations and exogenous disturbances. Traditional SMC methods suffer from chattering, which affects actuators and excites unmodelled high frequency dynamics. In the proposed design the sliding surface is constructed based on a Proportional-Derivative (PD) structure. Further Gao's reaching law is also integrated with SMC law to ensure faster convergence of the states to the sliding surface. The new techniques incorporate coulomb friction with saturation and deadband with relay to reduce the chattering level and scale down the control effort to minimum amount. Simulations demonstrates the tracking performance and improvement in chattering reduction for the proposed designs.

articleTitle: Text Simplification Using T5 Model and BART Model
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Text simplification is an important part of Natural Language Processing. It focuses on transforming complex text into simpler versions while preserving the meaning. This study examines the performance of two advanced models, T5 (Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer) and BART (Bidirectional and Auto-Regressive Transformers), in simplifying text. The models are trained on a dataset containing complex and simplified text pairs. Their performance is evaluated using BLEU, ROUGE, and SARI scores. The results show that both models perform well, but BART achieves better BLEU and ROUGE scores.

articleTitle: Determination of Maximum Load Handling Capacity with and Without DG Considering the Voltage Security
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: Traditional distribution networks face voltage instability and infrastructure overload due to urbanization and technology advances driving electricity consumption. Distributed Generation (DG) may solve these concerns. Considering voltage security limitations, this article calculates the maximum load handling capability of a Radial Distribution System (RDS) with and without DG. A comprehensive methodology is used to test loadability limits in a 118-bus RDS utilizing deterministic methods. Voltage stability and system maximum loadability are examined with and without DG inclusion. The deterministic approach was shown to accurately determine load handling capacity while maintaining voltage security. The computationally efficient and reliable approach for determining DG capacity gives vital insights for improving current distribution network efficiency. Findings help explain how DG integration might increase system resilience and operational efficiency in the face of rising energy needs.

articleTitle: A Review on Bioinformatics using DNA Cryptography
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: DNA-based encryption with bioinformatics has emerged as a promising field for secure data storage and transfer. This study analyzes the bioinformatics aspects of DNA cryptography, focusing on important advancements and challenges. We look at techniques like DNA origami, enzymatic reactions, and DNA strand displacement that use DNA sequences to encode and decode data. Additionally discussed are the security implications of DNA-based cryptography, including privacy issues, data integrity issues, and the potential for DNA-based attacks. Finally, we outline some possible directions for further review, such as developing more robust error-correction systems, looking at cutting-edge DNA-based encryption methods using bioinformatics, and addressing the ethical and societal implications of this emerging technology.

articleTitle: Advanced Machine Learning Techniques for Early Diagnosis of Diabetic Macular Edema
publicationTitle: 2025 8th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: One consequence of diabetic retinopathy is diabetic macular edema (DME), a condition that effects the eyes of individuals with diabetes. More than 28 million people been affecting by diabetic macular edema due to diabetes, late diagnose of diabetic macular edema leads to vision loss. Available method with deep learning algorithms and artificial intelligence (AI) for prediction of diabetic macular edema is not effective way for diagnosing in early. Proposed a method with XGBoost algorithm for the classification, pre-processing, extraction and detection of a disease by fundus samples. This method resulted in 0.992, 0.989, 0.991 and 0.990 for accuracy, Recall, precision and F1-score respectively.
